dependence on the aid is decreasing for this batch of characters

prohibited: Counting a correct reading with aid as knowing the character
Inferring that the learner can read it in any context from reading it right in this passage (especially not for polyphonic characters)
Inferring understanding of word meaning from a correct reading (such as Japanese 手紙)
Judging by machine whether reading aloud is right

hints: Only ask "in which character have you seen the component of this one?"
Show the same character in another word that the learner has already read right
Show the aid (the character is recorded as peeked at in this round)
scaffold.fade: This is the main body of the primitive: remove the aid when a character is read right without peeking in two rounds. After that, one more error restores it, and after restoring it needs two correct readings again. When the removal rate for the whole passage reaches 80%, the next passage has no aid by default and can only be viewed by tapping

primitives.reverseHalf: Not all aid should be removed: the readings of polyphonic characters in new contexts, jukujikun, and names of people and places must always be tappable. On the other hand, "can read it" does not mean "understands the meaning": Japanese 手紙 and 勉強, and Chinese homophone substitutions (再 / 在), can be read right while the meaning is still wrong, and the meaning question in Step 3 is there for this half

failureModes.failure: The learner peeks at every character before answering, and everything looks right
failureModes.mitigation: Answers after a peek never count as independent, and the removal condition looks only at answers without a peek
failureModes.test: Simulate a learner who peeks at everything, and check that the aid is not removed

failureModes.failure: The learner guesses the whole sentence from context and does not actually know the individual characters
failureModes.mitigation: The typed reading in the spot-check appears once, separate from the sentence
failureModes.test: Put the same character in a completely different sentence in another passage and spot-check again

failureModes.failure: Wrong aid data for polyphonic characters causes the wrong thing to be removed
failureModes.mitigation: Polyphonic characters are checked by hand one by one, and Step 2 provides the "special reading here" class
failureModes.test: Material check: the aid for polyphonic characters such as 还, 行, 长, 重, 了 in the material

stacksWith.how: For a character read wrong after the aid is removed, expand the character cell at its position in the original and split its components, without leaving this passage
A new character with its aid removed is first guessed from context, then the aid and gloss are shown. The guess and the reveal stay on the same character
In Chinese, remove the pinyin letters first and the tone marks later, and before the tone marks are removed do one contour judgment on the same character

Polyphonic characters, on'yomi / kun'yomi and jukujikun classed in Step 2 as "reading is special here" move to reading selection at the same position in the original, explaining why it is read this way here

languages.en: The aid layer is the sound-button dots and lines of the beginner stage and picture cues, used for decodable short texts for ages 5–8. Adults generally do not need it. Material comes from kt:en-orth-cvc-decoding, kt:en-orth-digraphs-blends, kt:en-orth-sight-words. Trap: the dots and lines of sight words do not follow the rules anyway and should be removed directly
languages.ja: The aid layer is furigana. The removal unit is the kanji word, not the single character, because the same kanji is read differently in different words. Material comes from kt:ja-kanji-n5 to n2, kt:ja-kanji-joyo. Trap: Chinese learners can understand the meaning but cannot read it out, so Step 1 must require typing the kana reading and cannot ask only the meaning question
languages.zh: The aid layer is pinyin (with tone marks), and it can be removed in two levels: remove the tone marks first and then the letters, or the reverse, as chosen by the teacher. Material comes from kt:zh-hanzi-l1 to l4. The main users are English-speaking adults and Chinese heritage children. Trap: heritage children are strong in speech and often guess the reading from the sentence, so they must be caught with single-character spot-checks

primitives.name: Word-shape splitting
primitives.oneLine: Cut a long or compound word into morphemes, check the meaning of the split, then bring out a family of words sharing the same morpheme
primitives.difficulty: Faced with a long or compound word, the learner either gives up on the whole word or memorizes the whole word, and never first looks for the part they know. At the other extreme is guessing from the surface: invaluable read as "worthless", 手紙 read as "toilet paper", 东西 read as "east and west". What the learner lacks is an action they can take with them: first find the piece you know, then check whether the meaning from the split can be trusted.
primitives.object: 3–6 words that can be split, each laid out letter by letter, kana by kana or character by character, with the cut marks drawn directly on the word. The family of words later brought out by the same morpheme is also hung below this word card
primitives.requires: Can recognize each letter, kana or character of these words (the meaning of the word need not be known), and knows the meaning of at least one piece. If the characters themselves cannot be recognized, fall back to prim:character-anatomy first
learnerAction: Step 1 Cut: tap a cut mark between letters or characters. Where it is cut right it becomes a vertical line, and when all cuts are done each piece floats up with its class and meaning. The word must be cut first before the "what does it mean" options appear

Step 2 Don't trust it fully: for 4–8 words, judge how the literal meaning from the split relates to the real meaning (locked options: split is right / exactly the opposite / the meaning lies elsewhere)
Step 3 Bring out a family: one morpheme is hidden in 4–6 words. Pick two and write a sentence of your own, and it must not be about the topic in the material
systemResponse: A correct cut becomes a vertical line, and below each piece a class label and meaning float up, for example un｜not, reverse; mistak｜get wrong; able｜can be …ed, makes an adjective

A wrong cut is not just called wrong; the system explains why it cannot be cut here: the piece on the left is nothing at all, there are only a limited number of prefixes or front-attached morphemes, look among them first

After Step 2 is judged, the literal meaning and the real meaning are shown side by side. In Step 3 the two words written are connected to the same morpheme node, and the word-family map grows with them

ui.screen: In the middle is a row of large letters or characters with thin gaps between them that can be tapped. Below is a floating layer of piece classes. The narrow right column is the word-family map for "this family". Step 2 is replaced by a word card with three judgment buttons
interactions: Tap a gap to cut, tap again to undo. Left and right arrow keys move between gaps, and Enter cuts
Step 2: number keys 1–3 choose the judgment
Step 3: type, and words in the family map can be tapped to insert them
ui.childVariant: Only two-piece words (compounds: sunflower, 雨傘, 火车), cuts shown with a scissors animation, and meaning shown with pictures. The judgment "exactly the opposite" is not used
ui.adultVariant: Choose academic or technical words (Greek and Latin roots, four-character Chinese words), show morpheme terminology and etymology, and Step 3 writes two sentences
ui.accessibility: The tappable area of the gaps is enlarged to touch-screen size. Screen readers read letter by letter and report "between character n and n+1". Piece classes are marked with both text and color

kcSignals: component is lexical or strategic and the label involves word formation, morphemes, roots or guessing from characters (such as kt:en-word-formation, kt:en-lex-greek-latin, kt:ja-kanji-system, kt:ja-str-guess-kanji, kt:zh-morphemes-compounds, kt:zh-str-guess-morphemes)
commonErrors include a wrongly chosen negative prefix (*unpossible) or examples of same-form-different-meaning and guessing from the surface
itemTypes include match or read-comprehend, and the target word is a compound or derived word
learnerSignals: Gives up on a long word at a glance
Memorizes roots and affixes and cannot use them
"Why is this word so long"
Reads Japanese kanji words by their Chinese character meanings
contraindications: The word cannot be split (single-morpheme words, jukujikun, such as 土産, 大人)
The meaning from the split has no link to the real meaning and the word is also a high-frequency basic word, so memorizing it directly is easier
The learner cannot yet recognize the letters or characters themselves

rules: Material check: the pieces joined together must exactly equal the original word. Every word has at least one core morpheme. Each of the four locked piece classes appears at least once, including the class "only for joining"
Material check: every word has at least one wrong-cut diagnosis, and the position of the diagnosis cannot fall on a real cut
Step 2: each of the three judgments appears at least once, with at least one "split is right", and they cannot all be "split is right"

Step 3: the sentence must contain two different words of the family (blocks an answer that is too weak); it must not fall on the forbidden topic, and must not overlap heavily with the example sentences in the material (blocks copying)
In Step 1 the position of the correct option must be shuffled, and not in the same position on every item
check.independence: The position of the first cut on each word is recorded separately. Cutting right after seeing the wrong-cut diagnosis is recorded as completed after hint. The first judgment in Step 2 is recorded separately

evidence.retained: The cut sequence for each word (including wrong-cut positions), the first judgment in Step 2, the learner's own sentences in Step 3, and the word family brought out by them

licensed.claim: can cut correct boundaries on morphemes that have been learned
when meeting a new word, looks first for morphemes they know, and is aware that the meaning from the split may not be reliable

prohibited: Judging that the word's meaning is understood because it was cut right
Inferring that the learner can produce the word from being able to split it
Inferring that the learner will not guess from the surface later because they judged "the meaning lies elsewhere" in Step 2

hints: First find the piece you know
List the limited number of prefixes or front-attached morphemes
Show a word of the same family that has already been cut
scaffold.fade: After three words in a row where the first cut is right, stop showing the morpheme list

primitives.reverseHalf: Splitting words can mislead: invaluable, inflammable, 手紙, 勉強, 东西, 马上. But there is also a reverse of the reverse: if you teach only that "splitting cannot be trusted", the learner will not dare to split from then on, and the loss is greater, because splitting works most of the time. So Step 2 has at least one "split is right", and the page says plainly "the following are exceptions, not the norm".

failureModes.failure: The learner taps every gap
failureModes.mitigation: Every wrong cut gets a diagnosis and is counted. When the number of cuts exceeds the number of pieces plus one, stop and have the learner undo first
failureModes.test: A sequence that taps every gap cannot pass Step 1

failureModes.failure: The examples are all traps, and the learner learns not to dare to split
failureModes.mitigation: Hard constraint: at least one "split is right"
failureModes.test: Material in which Step 2 is all opposite and elsewhere must fail the check

failureModes.failure: In Japanese, sound change is treated as a morpheme (学校 cut as がっ｜こう)
failureModes.mitigation: Provide a "junction sound change" class, and give the base form がく in the diagnosis
failureModes.test: Adversarial examples: 学校, 合鍵, 一緒; when cut at the sound-change point, the base-form hint is given

stacksWith.how: At the first encounter with a new word, cut it first, and use the meaning from the split as the candidate for the first bet. The next two encounters correct it
For languages written in Chinese characters, the same word card is split one more layer down, from morphemes to components
The word family brought out goes into the next batch of recall cards, with the morpheme as the cue

languages.en: The four piece classes pre/root/suf/link are locked, and the three judgments same/opposite/elsewhere are locked (c28). Trap words: invaluable, inflammable, outstanding, disinterested. Examples of link are speedometer, thermometer. Common errors are a wrongly chosen negative prefix (*unpossible, *unhonest) and singular/plural of Greek and Latin words (criterion/criteria). If blending is not yet secure, the step back is prim:sound-spelling-blend, not character-anatomy. Existing implementation c28
languages.ja: The object is kanji compounds (on'yomi morphemes) and native-Japanese compound verbs (取り出す). The four piece classes: front-attached morphemes (不・無・非・未・再), core morphemes, back-attached morphemes (〜的・〜性・〜化・〜者・〜家, which fix the word class), and junction sound change (gemination 学＋校→がっこう, rendaku 合＋鍵→あいかぎ, which changes only the sound and carries no meaning). The traps are mainly Chinese-Japanese false friends: 手紙, 勉強, 大家, 留守, 迷惑, 検討. Jukujikun are listed separately as "cannot be cut"
languages.zh: The object is multi-character compound words, and the learners are English native speakers. Piece classes: modifying morphemes, head morphemes, affix-like morphemes (-者, -员, -家, -化, -性, 可-, 非-), and bleached morphemes (the 子 of 桌子, the 头 of 石头, the 老 of 老虎, which have no real meaning and correspond to English link). Step 1 can add a layer of structure judgment: modifier-head (偏正), verb-object (动宾), coordinate (并列), subject-predicate (主谓), complement (补充). Traps: 东西, 马上, 救火, 地道. For separable words (见面, 帮忙), after cutting, a hint shows where the object goes

primitives.name: Recall before reveal
primitives.oneLine: First retrieve the wording from a blank and keep the first answer, then reveal and compare, recording independent and after-hint answers separately
primitives.difficulty: The learner recognizes it on sight but cannot say it. Review is just "looking again", so the illusion of "I know it" grows stronger. What was learned is forgotten, and at the next review the learner does not know which items to look at. Multiple choice and flipping cards produce almost no retrieval, and the learner is never asked to pull something out of a blank.
primitives.object: A batch of 8–12 items that the learner really studied earlier (chunks, collocations, kana and kanji, verb forms), each with a situation cue. The first answers, the results of two rounds and the list "only these few next time" are all kept on this set of cards, and review across sessions keeps using the same set of cards
primitives.requires: The learner studied these items before (from the chunk book, scenes, usage judge, and so on). Items never studied cannot be put in: failing to recall what was never learned is not review, it is making things hard. In that case, fall back to prim:chunk-harvest to teach first
learnerAction: Step 1 Blind first round: only the situation cue, the meaning in the learner's own language, and a sentence start with a gap (or the reading, or the dictionary form) are given, with no options. Write or say it. Leaving it blank counts too

Step 2 Compare and grade: the system judges recalled / almost / not recalled (three locked levels), and the answer is laid out beside what the learner wrote. The second round retests only the items not written out, with one more line of first-letter hint

Step 3 String them together and schedule: pick three or more items and write a short piece about your own life. Items not recalled, or recalled only after a hint, go into "only these few next time" and come back at intervals; next time it again starts from blank
systemResponse: The answer column on the right is blurred at first and becomes clear only after comparison. Two dots after each item record the results of the two rounds
When an item is judged "almost", the system gives a diagnosis of the wrong road the learner took (for example give me pressure is a literal translation of "give"), and not only the answer
The list is scheduled at intervals (for example 1 day, 3 days, 7 days). At the next opening only items that are due come up, in shuffled order, mixed with items from other sources

ui.screen: One card at a time: at the top is the situation cue and the meaning in the learner's own language, in the middle is a sentence start with one gap and an empty input box, and below is a "compare" button. On the right is a table of blurred answers for all items in the batch with the dots for the two rounds. The end page is the "only these few next time" list, and does not show accuracy
interactions: Enter to compare, Tab to jump to the next item
Tapping compare with the box empty also counts as completing the item
In Step 3, items in the list can be tapped to insert a reminder (the answer is not inserted)
ui.childVariant: Items are replaced by picture plus word, or kana or kanji, said aloud, with a parent or teacher tapping "recalled / almost". Each batch has 5–6 items, and intervals are shown with a sticker calendar
ui.adultVariant: Cues are written as specific situations from work or life. Step 3 writes an email or message of five or six sentences, and the list can be exported to a calendar
ui.accessibility: The blur effect is accompanied by the text state "not revealed". The dots also use the symbols ✓ ~ ○ for the three levels. The input box works with the candidate windows of Japanese and Chinese input methods, and does not judge early while the spelling is still being composed

kcSignals: component is lexical or orthographic, or a form that needs to be retrieved (such as kt:en-irregular-past, kt:en-collocation, kt:ja-te-form, kt:ja-kanji-n5, kt:zh-hanzi-l2, kt:zh-lex-measure-extended)
itemTypes include form-fill, dictation or script-writing
The KC has already been taught on the path and now needs review
learnerSignals: Forgets what was learned
Recognizes it on sight but cannot say it
Reviewed but with no effect
"What was taught last week is gone again this week"
contraindications: The learner has never studied the item
A single isolated word that cannot be written out in context and cannot be judged accurately: change it to a phrase
More than 20 items at a time: split into batches

rules: The cue and the sentence start must not contain the answer or the stem of the answer. Each sentence has only one gap. No options are offered

Matching of accepted answers must be lenient: variants, upper and lower case, full-width and half-width forms, and kana and kanji spellings all count. The standard answer must pass its own matching. The trap rule for "almost" must not wrongly hit the answers of other items
"Recalled" is given only to a first answer made without seeing a hint. A blank, a copy of only the cue, or writing only the first letter that the hint gives is judged "not recalled" (blocks gaming)
Step 3 must use at least three items, and must not copy a whole example sentence from a card
Across sessions: an item may leave the list only after independent first answers of "recalled" on at least two occasions more than one day apart
check.independence: The first answer in each review is recorded separately. An answer in the second round with the first-letter hint is recorded as completed after hint. First answers on different days are the main source of independent evidence

evidence.retained: For each item each time: the original text of the first answer, the level judged, whether a hint was seen, the interval in days, and the list "only these few next time"

licensed.claim: this item could be retrieved independently from blank in this review
this item can still be retrieved independently the next day
can actively use these items in a paragraph they write themselves

prohibited: Judging long-term mastery from recalling it in one review
Counting second-round answers with a hint as independent
Treating "almost" as never studied and teaching the whole item again
Ranking learners by the length of the list

hints: Reread the situation cue: who were you speaking to then, and why
A first-letter hint (t… f… g…, the first kana, the first letter of the pinyin)
Show the length slots of the answer: how many words, moras or characters
scaffold.fade: After an item is recalled on its first answer on two different days in a row, the second round no longer gives the first-letter hint. Next time only the meaning in the learner's own language is given and the sentence start is no longer given, so the cue goes from strong to weak

primitives.reverseHalf: Leaving it blank is better than guessing: not recalling is not failure, it is exactly what this page is looking for. "Almost" is not wrong either: the learner did recall it and only took a wrong road, so give a diagnosis of the wrong road, not the answer. On the other side, continuing frequent review of items that can already be retrieved stably is a waste, so the list must be able to "graduate" items.

failureModes.failure: The cue leaks the answer (words with the same root, the same character in a Chinese-character word)
failureModes.mitigation: Check that the cue does not contain the answer or its stem or the characters in the answer
failureModes.test: Adversarial example: a cue written as "当成理所当然" (taken as a matter of course) with the answer take for granted is allowed; if granted appears in the cue it must raise an error

failureModes.failure: Answer matching is too narrow, and a correct answer is judged not recalled
failureModes.mitigation: The standard answer must pass its own matching. Add variants for contractions, full-width forms and two spellings
failureModes.test: Test with I'd, ｔａｋｅ (full-width), and both spellings きょう / 今日, and all must be judged recalled

failureModes.failure: In spaced review the order and cues do not change, and the learner remembers positions
failureModes.mitigation: Shuffle the order each time and change the situation cue
failureModes.test: The cue text for the same item must differ between two reviews

stacksWith.how: After a scene has been walked through, walking it a second time from memory is this primitive acting on the same timeline
Items in the chunk book become recall cards directly, and the recall result is written back to the chunk book
Form recall cards: give the dictionary form and the name of the target form, and write the conjugated form. When "almost", show each step of the rule derivation

languages.en: Items are mostly chunks and collocations (take sth for granted, put pressure on) and irregular past tense and past participles (went/gone). The three levels got/close/blank are locked (c12). Typical traps are *give me pressure and *have went. The existing implementation c12 covers only two rounds of a single review plus an exported list, with no scheduling across sessions, so the status is partial
languages.ja: Three kinds of cards: (1) kana-kanji recall: give the reading and write the kanji, or give the kanji and write the reading (今日 is きょう, not こんにち), and matching accepts both kana and kanji spellings; (2) conjugation recall: give the dictionary form and the target form (て-form, ない-form, potential form) and write it out; 書く→書いて, and writing *書きて is judged "almost" and shows the euphonic-change rule; (3) chunk recall: お風呂に入る, 傘をさす. The first-letter hint becomes the first kana
languages.zh: The learners are English native speakers, and cues are written in English. Three kinds of cards: (1) character recall: give pinyin and context and write the character, and homophone characters (再/在, 已/己) are judged "almost"; (2) tone recall: give the character and write toned pinyin, and tone errors are recorded separately; (3) collocation and measure-word recall: 提高水平, 解决问题 (*提高问题 is judged "almost"), 一件衣服 (*一个衣服). The first-letter hint becomes the first letter of the pinyin or the radical

primitives.name: Chunk harvest & collocation
primitives.oneLine: Pick out phrases and collocations worth remembering from real material, collect them in your own chunk book, and try each one once
primitives.difficulty: The learner can understand a passage but cannot use any of the phrases in it. They memorize isolated words, and what they write is translated word by word from their first language: *make homework, *big rain, *お風呂を入ります, *提高问题. Each word is right on its own, so a dictionary does not find the error. The learner does not know which words come in strings, or who a word's partners are.
primitives.object: A passage of real material (200–500 words or characters) and the chunk book the learner collects from it. The same chunk book is used throughout trying and the learner's own writing. For the collocation-web variant, the object is one core noun and a ring of candidate partners around it
primitives.requires: The learner understands the gist of the material. If too many unknown words get in the way, fall back to prim:context-guess for triage first, or change the material
learnerAction: Step 1 Harvest: tap the phrases worth remembering in the original text (an underline appears on mouse-over). Look at the meaning, usage, new example sentences and common first-language transfer errors on the card, then collect it into the chunk book, at least three. Collocation-web variant: open one locked position at a time and find the partners that can go with the core word

Step 2 Try: test only the chunks you collected. Each item is a new situation unrelated to the original plus a gap to fill, and the distractors are phrasings translated directly from the first language. If you choose wrong, you get a diagnosis for the one you chose
Step 3 Write your own: a real writing situation, where the chunk book becomes a row of buttons. Use three or more to write a paragraph of your own
systemResponse: Harvested chunks light up in the original text, fly into the chunk book on the right, and are labeled with the class they belong to

Candidates in the collocation web that cannot connect are crossed out, and the card explains in three parts: why your first language made you think so, how the target language actually says it, and what to watch for next time. This item also accumulates into the list "first-language traps you have stepped on"
The distractors in try items are exactly the ones you just connected wrongly. When writing your own, the chunks you used are highlighted in the text, and the chunk book counts this item

ui.screen: On the left is the original text, on the right the chunk book and the card. In the collocation-web variant, the middle holds the core word with a ring of candidates, and the top says which position is being sought now. Step 3 changes to a writing box with a row of chunk buttons above it. The lower-right corner holds the first-language trap list. No score is given
interactions: Hover with the mouse to bring up the underline, click to open the card, Enter to collect it into the chunk book
In the collocation web, click a candidate to draw a connection, and Tab moves between candidates
Step 3: tap a button to insert the chunk at the cursor, or type it yourself
ui.childVariant: Material becomes a picture-book page or a rhyme. Chunks are limited to two classes (fixed phrases, word collocations), two are collected each time, trying becomes choosing from a picture, and Step 3 becomes saying one sentence aloud
ui.adultVariant: Material is taken from foreign-language periodicals, work emails and podcast transcripts, with the five class terms shown. Step 3 writes an email or a comment
ui.accessibility: The underline also has a dashed style and does not rely on color alone. All phrases that can be harvested can be visited in turn by keyboard. The card content can be read by a screen reader in sections: "meaning, usage, examples, caution"

kcSignals: component is lexical and the label involves collocation, phrasal verbs, idioms or topic vocabulary (such as kt:en-collocation, kt:en-adjective-collocation, kt:en-phrasal-basic, kt:ja-lex-daily-verbs, kt:ja-lex-yojijukugo-idioms, kt:zh-lex-abstract-collocation, kt:zh-lex-l3-core)
commonErrors include collocation errors translated directly from a first-language verb
itemTypes include match, form-fill and situated-production-written
learnerSignals: Memorized the word list and still cannot use it
The sentences they write are clearly translated from the first language
Cannot recall "how that sentence should be said"
Cannot tell make/do/take apart
contraindications: There are too many new words in the material, and the learner cannot understand the gist
The target is only recognizing single words, not using them in strings
There are no portable phrases in the material (all proper names and numbers)

rules: Material check: each chunk must appear in the original text exactly as written. The example sentences on the card must not come from the original text and must be in a new context. The context of a try item must not be too like the original text

Material check: chunks must cover at least two classes, to stop the learner thinking "a chunk is a verb phrase". Every distractor needs a diagnosis written. In the collocation web the numbers that can connect and cannot connect must not be far apart, and each position has at least one first-language trap

Step 3: at least three must be used (matching must allow inflection and conjugation), this blocks an answer that is too weak. It must also not copy a whole example sentence from the card or the original text, and must not contain a first-language direct-translation trap already marked, this blocks gaming
When three chunks are crowded into one sentence, prompt "use them in different sentences"
check.independence: Harvesting is the learner's own choice and is not judged right or wrong. The first choice in a try item is recorded separately. In writing, a chunk inserted by tapping a button is recorded as "inserted", and only one typed by the learner counts as used independently

evidence.retained: The chunk book: the items harvested, the source sentences, the first choice in try items, the number and manner of uses in writing (inserted or typed), and the list "first-language traps you have stepped on"

licensed.claim: can recognize the correct form of this chunk in a new context
can use this chunk independently in their own writing

prohibited: Treating the number harvested as the number acquired
Counting insertion by button as independent production
Judging that the learner can use an item because they chose right on a try item

hints: Tell the learner "there are N phrases in this passage that can be carried away as a block"
Show the underlines faintly in the original text
Open the card for one item directly
scaffold.fade: After more than half of the chunks the learner harvested independently from two materials in a row overlap with the reference list, stop showing the faint underlines

primitives.reverseHalf: Not every common combination is worth collecting: free combinations (read a book, 本を読む, 买东西) need only the individual words, and when tapped the page says "this is a free combination". Nor is every direct translation wrong: make a plan / 做计划 and お茶を飲む / 喝茶 happen to match. Every trap list puts in at least one example where "the direct translation is also right", so that the learner does not learn "every direct translation is wrong".

failureModes.failure: The learner taps every new word into the chunk book, and the chunk book becomes a vocabulary list
failureModes.mitigation: Only preset chunks can be collected. When a single new word or a free combination is tapped, explain why it is not collected
failureModes.test: Tapping the words bread, パン or 面包 must not put them into the chunk book

failureModes.failure: When writing their own, the learner piles in chunks to make up the number
failureModes.mitigation: Require the chunks to be spread across different sentences and the total length to meet the minimum
failureModes.test: A submission that crams three chunks into one sentence triggers a prompt

failureModes.failure: The distractors are not phrasings the learner would really write
failureModes.mitigation: At least half of the distractors come from the first-language direct translations in the commonErrors of the matching KC
failureModes.test: Spot-check that the overlap between the distractors and commonErrors is no less than half

stacksWith.how: After a few days, items in the chunk book become recall cards, and the results are written back to the chunk book
Take the item in the chunk book that keeps being used wrongly and use it for a usage judgment
After Step 3, move the chunk book's items to a matter of the learner's own life unrelated to the original material

languages.en: The five chunk classes verb/phrase/frame/colloc/discourse are locked (c02). The collocation web has four positions verb/adj/prep/noun, and the core word is a noun only (c05). Typical traps: *big pressure, *give me pressure, *do a decision, *big rain. Existing implementations c02, c05
languages.ja: Five chunk classes: verb collocations (noun + particle + verb: お風呂に入る, 傘をさす, 熱が出る), fixed expressions (よろしくお願いします, お疲れ様です), sentence frames (〜ば〜ほど, 〜というより), word collocations (大雨, 濃いお茶, ぐっすり眠る), connecting expressions (それにしても, とはいえ). The collocation-web positions become: noun + を / に / が + verb, adjective + noun, noun + の + noun, mimetic word + verb. Traps come from direct translation from Chinese and carrying kanji words over directly (*お風呂を入ります, *テニスを遊びます)
languages.zh: The learners are English native speakers. Five chunk classes: verb-object collocations (解决问题, 取得进步, 作出决定), fixed phrases (chengyu, idioms), sentence frames (越…越…, 连…都…), measure-word-noun and adjective-noun collocations (一件衣服, 浓茶, 大雨), discourse connectors (另外, 总之, 说实话). The collocation-web positions become: verb + it, adjective + it, measure word + it, noun + it. Traps come from direct translation from English (*制造决定, *做进步, *吃汤, *玩钢琴)

primitives.name: Usage boundary judging
primitives.oneLine: For several uses of a word or a group of near-synonyms, judge one by one whether you can say it that way, assign each error to a boundary class, then make your own sentence
primitives.difficulty: The learner knows what the word means but keeps making errors with the same word: suggest me to, discuss about, *帮忙我, *我知道他 (meaning to say "I know him"), *電車を乗ります, *魚を好きです. Checking a dictionary does not fix it, because a dictionary gives the meaning, not "what cannot follow". The mark of being able to use a word is knowing its boundary.
primitives.object: One word the learner keeps using wrongly (or a group of near-synonyms), and 6–8 sentences attached to it. A usage map on the right lists 3–5 uses of the word, and each use lights up as soon as a sentence for it has been judged
primitives.requires: Knows the basic meaning of the word. If even the meaning is not known, fall back to prim:chunk-harvest first and meet the word in material
learnerAction: Step 1 Judge: for each sentence, decide whether you can say it that way. For those judged "cannot", choose which class the error belongs to (five locked classes: wrong form / wrong sense / wrong collocation / wrong situation / wrong strength)
Step 2 Re-judge: change only the sentences you just judged cannot be said, in free input. The system points out which known old habit you stepped on
Step 3 Use it yourself: a real writing situation that requires using the word in more than one use
systemResponse: A sentence that has been judged attaches to the matching use on the usage map, and that use goes from gray to lit

When the learner judges "can say" but it actually cannot be said, the system does not give the answer directly, only a pointer (the problem is not in the second half of the sentence; look at the two words right next to this word). When the learner judges "cannot" but it actually can, it explains at once why it holds

When the class is chosen wrong, it explains what this class really means and why this sentence does not belong to it. When a re-judgment steps on an old habit again, it points out exactly which one. When the fix is right, it gives another way to fix it

ui.screen: At the top is the target word, and below it a column of 6–8 sentence cards. Each card has two buttons, "can say / cannot say", and after "cannot" is chosen five class buttons open. On the right is the usage map. In the lower right corner, "my judgments" records how many sentences were judged the wrong way and which class is most often chosen wrongly. No score is given
interactions: Y/N keys to judge, number keys 1–5 to choose the class
Step 2: edit directly inside the sentence card
A "show me one way to fix it" button sits at the bottom of the re-judging area
ui.childVariant: One high-frequency word with four sentences, only judging "can say / cannot say", with no five classes. A wrong sentence uses a picture to show what is wrong, and Step 3 is saying one sentence aloud
ui.adultVariant: Choose words that really go wrong in the learner's writing, with sentences taken from the learner's own essays (anonymized), the five class terms shown, and Step 3 writes a paragraph of three or four sentences
ui.accessibility: All five class buttons are always shown, in fixed positions. Right and wrong feedback also has text, not only color. The usage map can be expanded item by item by keyboard

kcSignals: component is lexical and the label involves near-synonym discrimination, precise word choice, false friends (such as kt:en-lexical-precision, kt:en-false-friends, kt:ja-ga-subject, kt:ja-lex-word-origin, kt:zh-synonym-discrimination, kt:zh-lixin-ci)
commonErrors show two or more kinds of error for the same word
itemTypes include error-correct and recognize-choice
learnerSignals: Keeps getting the same word wrong
Checked the dictionary and still got it wrong
"Can this word really be used this way?"
contraindications: The learner does not even know the basic meaning of the word
The word has only one use and one way of going wrong, and prim:choose-by-intent or a single correction is enough
The so-called "error" is only a dialect or a variant acceptable in speech

rules: Material check: 6–8 sentences, at least 2 that can be said and at least 3 that cannot. The wrong sentences must not all be of one class. Each sentence has at least two class diagnoses that learners would really choose wrongly
Material check: sentences that can be said must not be misjudged by the trap rules of Step 3. The matching rule for each use on the usage map must match its own example sentence
Step 3: matching must hit two different uses (blocks an answer that is too weak), and the text must not step on the old habit or copy a sentence from the material (blocks gaming)
Step 2: the rewrite must still contain the target word. Deleting the target word to avoid the error does not pass
check.independence: The first judgment in Step 1 (whether it can be said, plus the class) is recorded separately. Judging right after seeing the pointer is recorded as completed after hint. A rewrite after tapping "show me one way to fix it" is recorded as answer seen

evidence.retained: For each sentence: the first judgment, the re-judgment and the class choice; the lighting of the usage map; the learner's own sentences in Step 3; and the "my judgments" statistics

licensed.claim: can recognize the main error boundaries of this word
can use two or more uses of this word correctly in their own production

prohibited: Inferring that production will no longer go wrong because all the judgment items were right
Treating a wrongly chosen class as the same as a wrongly judged sentence
Extrapolating the result for one word to its near-synonyms

hints: The problem is not in the second half of the sentence; look at the two words right after this word
Show the form of the relevant use on the usage map
Give a sentence that can be said and differs by only one place, for comparison
scaffold.fade: After the first judgments and the classes are all right for the same word in two materials in a row, Step 2 no longer gives a pointer

primitives.reverseHalf: Every material has at least two sentences that look wrong but can be said (suggest that he take…, a variant acceptable in speech), and someone who taps "cannot" all the way will be stopped by them. The five class buttons are always all shown, and a word usually steps on only two or three of them. The classes not stepped on are the distractors, and each must explain "why this sentence does not belong to this class".

failureModes.failure: The learner taps "cannot" all the way and gets through by guessing
failureModes.mitigation: At least two sentences that can be said, with the proportion close
failureModes.test: An answer sequence that taps "cannot" for everything must be stopped on at least two sentences

failureModes.failure: The learner chooses the class by surface keywords (sees a formal word and chooses "wrong situation")
failureModes.mitigation: Each error class has at least one sentence whose surface cue points to another class
failureModes.test: Adversarial example: a sentence that contains hereby but is actually wrong in form

failureModes.failure: When re-judging, the learner replaces the target word to avoid the problem
failureModes.mitigation: The rewrite must still contain the target word
failureModes.test: A rewrite that changes suggest to ask must not pass

stacksWith.how: A near-synonym group (以为/认为, あげる/くれる) is switched on the same context card, to see how the meaning changes after the word changes
The core noun in a collocation-type wrong sentence moves to the collocation web, to find its partners in the four positions
Errors with the same word in the learner's essay are fixed one of the five classes at a time

languages.en: The five classes form/sense/partner/register/strength are locked (c04). When the judgment is uncertain, go in the order form→sense→partner→strength→register. Typical words: suggest, explain, discuss, marry, economic. Existing implementation c04
languages.ja: The five classes become: wrong connection or particle (*電車を乗ります, *魚を好きです, *会社に働きます), wrong sense (Chinese-Japanese same-form words: 勉強, 迷惑, 結構), wrong collocation (*ぐっすり起きる, *テニスを遊びます), wrong register or honorific (*私がいらっしゃいます, saying ごめんなさい to a superior), wrong strength of tone (かもしれない / にちがいない). Typical words: 会う, 好き, わかる, 入る, あげる
languages.zh: The learners are English native speakers, and the explanation is written in English. The five classes become: wrong sentence pattern (a separable word with an object *见面你, *帮忙我), wrong sense (*我知道他, 经验/经历), wrong collocation (*提高问题, *制造决定), wrong register (*我们优化一下晚饭吧), wrong connotation or strength (positive/negative connotation: 导致/使, 无所不为; 严峻/严重). Typical words: 帮忙, 认识, 了解/理解, 以为/认为

primitives.name: Scene walkthrough
primitives.oneLine: Walk through an everyday scene from start to end, retrieving the words and sentences needed at each step, then walk it again from memory with a different turn of events
primitives.difficulty: The learner can recite the word list but cannot get the thing done. Words sorted by the same class (colors in one group, jobs in one group, body parts in one group) interfere with each other the closer their meanings are. When the scene arrives the learner goes dumb, or carries over a step and a phrasing from the first language directly: *register a number (挂号), *頭が疼い, *我有头疼.
primitives.object: One thing the learner will really meet, cut into a timeline of 4–6 moments (seeing a doctor: phone call → describe symptoms → take temperature → prescription → collect medicine). The word cluster of this scene accumulates on the right in four role cells, and all three passes run on the same line
primitives.requires: Knows most of the basic words in the scene, or has pictures to support them. If none of the basic words is known, fall back to prim:chunk-harvest first and collect words from material
learnerAction: Step 1 Walk through: the timeline lights up one step at a time. Read the situation and choose, in the gap in the sentence, the one sentence to say at this step (four choices, the distractors mostly from first-language direct translation)
Step 2 Walk again from memory: walk the same scene once more, with no options, only the situation and an empty input box. After writing, compare and judge recalled / almost / not recalled
Step 3 Change the course: events go another way (cannot get an appointment, the medicine is sold out), and the learner says or writes 5–7 sentences using this word cluster
systemResponse: When it is said right: it gives the explanation, a rule that can be taken away, and words that "also appear together at this step". These words fall into the four role cells on the right (who is in the scene / what is in hand / what to do / the state at the time)

When it is said wrong: it tells the learner what situation that phrasing actually belongs to, or explains that it was carried over directly from the first language and the target language does not have this step
Scene words used in Step 3 light up in the word cluster. The exported record marks those not recalled in the second pass, and the learner looks only at these few a few days later

ui.screen: At the top is a horizontal timeline with the current step highlighted. In the middle are the situation description and a sentence with a gap. Below are the options or an input box. On the right is the four-cell word cluster. No score is given
interactions: Number keys 1–4 to choose, Enter to compare
Left and right arrow keys to look back between moments already walked
Step 3: type or record, and words in the word cluster can be tapped to insert them
ui.childVariant: Scenes become going to school, a birthday, going to the park, buying ice cream. The timeline uses pictures, there are at most two options and they are read aloud, and Step 3 becomes looking at a picture and saying three sentences
ui.adultVariant: Scenes are reporting a repair on a rented flat, opening a bank account, seeing a doctor, returns and exchanges, starting a new job. Step 3 writes a paragraph of five to seven sentences, or is a role-play between two people
ui.accessibility: The timeline has both numbers and text labels. The four cells of the word cluster are told apart by titles, not by color alone. All images have alternative text

kcSignals: component is topic or functional, and the label is an everyday scene (such as kt:en-topic-health, kt:en-topic-housing, kt:ja-lex-body-health, kt:ja-lex-housing, kt:zh-lex-body-health, kt:zh-lex-transport-places)
commonErrors include phrasings translated directly from a first-language scene
itemTypes include role-play and situated-production-spoken
learnerSignals: Goes dumb when the scene arrives
Can recite the word list but cannot get the thing done
Wants to go through it first before going abroad or running an errand
"I'm going to see a doctor next week, how do I say it?"
contraindications: What is to be taught is a group of near-synonyms that need fine distinction (putting them together is then actually necessary, and prim:usage-boundary is used)
The scene is not real for the learner's age or situation (teaching renting a flat to a child)
The scene cannot be cut into 4 or more steps

rules: Material check: 4–6 moments; all four role cells must have words; at least 10 words in the whole scene

Material check: at least half of the moments have distractors that come from first-language direct translation, that is, phrasings the learner would really write, and every distractor has a diagnosis. The answer must not appear in the Step 2 cue

Step 3: at least three scene words must be used (blocks an answer that is too weak); also the text must not contain a first-language direct-translation trap, must not copy the original sentences of Step 1, and must write about the changed course (blocks gaming)
check.independence: The first choice in Step 1 is recorded separately. The blind writing in Step 2 is independent evidence. In Step 3 the word-cluster buttons are folded away by default, and opening them or inserting from them is recorded as completed after hint

evidence.retained: The first choice at each step on the timeline, the level at each step in the second pass, the paragraph from Step 3, and the lit-up state of the four-cell word cluster

licensed.claim: can retrieve the key phrasing for each step in the standard course of this scene
can organize these phrasings in another course of the same scene

prohibited: Extrapolating to other scenes
Treating a correct four-choice answer in Step 1 as being able to say it
Treating being able to write in Step 3 as the same as being able to say it in a real situation under time pressure

hints: Reread the situation at this moment and ask yourself "what do I need to do right now"
Point out which cell's words this step needs (you need a word for "what to do")
Give the first word of this sentence
scaffold.fade: When the same scene is entered a second time, skip Step 1 and start directly from walking from memory

primitives.reverseHalf: A step that exists in the first language may not exist at all in the target-language scene (registering at the hospital in English is just book an appointment; the Chinese 挂号 is an extra step for English-speaking learners); conversely, a target-language scene also has steps the first language lacks (in Japan, seeing a doctor starts with filling in a 問診票). Every scene has at least one moment where "this step does not exist or is different on their side". Step 3 must change the course, and cannot simply retell the original line.

failureModes.failure: The designer puts four near-synonymous phrasings together as options, and it goes back to same-class distraction
failureModes.mitigation: Distractors come from different situations or from first-language direct translation, not from a pile of near-synonyms
failureModes.test: The four options at one moment must not all come from the same semantic class

failureModes.failure: In Step 3 the learner recites the original line
failureModes.mitigation: Check the overlap with the original sentences of Step 1, and require the key words of the course to be written
failureModes.test: A submission copying the sentences of Step 1 is stopped

failureModes.failure: The word cluster is changed to be sorted by part of speech
failureModes.mitigation: The four role cells are locked, sorted by function in the event
failureModes.test: An error is raised when role names such as noun/verb appear in the material

stacksWith.how: Step 2 is the recall primitive acting on the same timeline, and words not recalled go into the recall list
The timeline becomes dialogue turns, and the other side's reaction branches according to the learner's choice
The moment in the scene where "it is different on their side" is expanded into a small misunderstanding incident

languages.en: The four roles who/thing/do/how are locked (c06). Scenes: seeing a doctor (*I head hurt), reporting a repair on a rented flat (*The light is bad), the bank (take out money), returns and exchanges. Existing implementation c06
languages.ja: Scenes: convenience-store checkout (袋はいりますか, 温めますか), seeing a doctor (問診票, 保険証; *頭が疼い should be 頭が痛い), asking the way, renting a flat (大家, 家賃, 敷金礼金; these same-form-different-meaning kanji words go into the traps), ordering food (*三名様です is using a shop assistant's honorific for yourself). The honorific language of the shop-assistant side needs only to be understood, not produced
languages.zh: The learners are English native speakers, and the situation descriptions are written in English. Scenes: ordering takeaway and paying by QR code, seeing a doctor (挂号; *我有头疼 should be 我头疼), taking the metro (*我出了公共汽车 should be 下车), renting a flat, ordering in a restaurant (measure words: 一碗, 一盘). Direct-translation traps come from English (*吃汤 should be 喝汤, *玩钢琴 should be 弹钢琴)

primitives.name: Classifier matching
primitives.oneLine: Choose the classifier, counter or countability marking by the shape or class of the thing, learn the pattern first, then handle exceptions and sound changes
primitives.difficulty: To count things, a word chosen by the class of the thing has to go between the number and the noun, or one first has to decide whether the noun can be counted directly. The learner's first language divides this differently. English native speakers say "三书" (three books) and "这学生" (this student), and after learning classifiers use 个 for everything (一个衣服, 一个水). Japanese native speakers carry "一本笔" and "一枚纸" into Chinese by their counters. Chinese learners of Japanese say 一瓶 for 一瓶啤酒 by Chinese habit, say 三つのりんご in Chinese word order, and misread いっぽん / さんぼん / ろっぽん and ひとり / ふたり. Chinese learners of English do not tell countable from uncountable and say *two breads, *an advice, *informations, *How many money, *a little apples, *less people, *some apple, because Chinese nouns themselves do not mark countability.
primitives.object: An item table: a dozen or so object pictures (book, paper, pen, umbrella, clothes, shoes, fish, water, rice, bread, money, advice, information, computer…) and a row of "counting-method" boxes. For Chinese these are classifiers, for Japanese counters, and for English "count directly (a/two/many/few)", "cannot count directly (much/little/less)" and container units (a cup of, a piece of, a loaf of). The learner puts items into boxes, and the same table then becomes a shopping list or an order
primitives.requires: The learner already knows the nouns for most items on the table and the numbers 1–10. Japanese sound-change items need media. If the nouns are not known, first bring the words out with prim:scene-walkthrough
learnerAction: Step 1 Sort into boxes: drag the items on the table into counting-method boxes, then for each box choose one shared feature from the locked list (flat / long and thin / paired / a set / bound volume / has a handle / machine / person; for English: can be counted one by one / is a mass or a kind / needs a container or unit to count)

Step 2 Classify new items: choose a box for an item not seen before. The locked options are: follows the pattern / outside the pattern and must be remembered separately / both are possible but meaning or tone differs / no classifier or unit is used here. The last two are the reverse half (一把伞, 一条新闻, Japanese 本 used for phone calls and films, 一个人 / 一位老师; English a coffee meaning a cup, chicken uncountable as food but countable as an animal, hair versus a hair). Japanese items also require choosing the reading of the number and counter together (いっぽん・にほん・さんぼん). English items, after the box is chosen, also require choosing the determiner for the item: many / much, a few / a little, fewer / less, whether some is followed by a plural or an uncountable

Step 3 Place your own order: for a real task (buying breakfast for the whole family, ordering at an izakaya, writing a shopping list, asking "how much do you want"), write sentences with quantities. Word order and form must fit the language (Japanese N を quantity V, Chinese number + classifier + noun, English two loaves of bread, How much milk, a few eggs)
systemResponse: When an item goes into a box, the feature label on the box lights up and shows what the items already in the box have in common. An item put into a general-purpose box such as 个 or つ is not judged wrong but marked yellow, with "understood, but more commonly said …" beside it. In English items, when an uncountable item is put into the "count directly" box, the picture of the item turns into a heap and not a single one, with a comparison of *two breads and two loaves of bread beside it
After a Japanese sound item is chosen, the combined reading of the number and counter is shown in kana, the moras that change (っ, ぼ, ぴ) are colored, and the recording is played

The sentences of Step 3 are laid out line by line below as a list. On each line the classifier is connected by a line to the item on the table. Lines not connected, or connected to the wrong box, are marked

ui.screen: The upper half of the screen is the item table (a picture grid), and the lower half is a row of classifier boxes (3–6) with optional feature labels on the boxes. In Step 3 the lower half becomes the list. The right column records "how many times 个 / つ was used in this round"
interactions: Drag items into boxes, or select an item and press the box number
Tab moves between items, number keys put into a box
Step 3: type, or tap from three columns (number, classifier, noun) to build a sentence
ui.childVariant: Chinese heritage children (ages 6–12): made as a "classifier shop" where the child is the shop assistant. A customer (by voice) says "我要两……鞋", and the child puts the shoes in the 双 basket. At first there are only 2–3 boxes (个, 只, 本), then more are added step by step. For children who use 个 for everything in speech, the yellow hint is said by a cartoon character. Ages 5–7: only two boxes such as 张 / 本 or 只 / 条, all in pictures and recordings. English ages 5–7: a cup of / a slice of / a bowl of with food pictures on a breakfast plate, oral only and no writing. Ages 8–12 add two boxes, "can count one by one / a big heap", with an ordering dialogue of How many apples? / How much milk?
ui.adultVariant: Material comes from menus, supermarket receipts and business-trip purchase lists. Classifier class names and an exception table can be shown. Japanese adults have one more column, "the native-Japanese numerals ひとつ… work for everything", for judging when a specific counter can be skipped
ui.accessibility: Item pictures have text labels. Drag and drop has a keyboard alternative. Boxes are told apart by number as well as color

kcSignals: notions include quantity, and the KC is classifiers / counters / countability and quantity determiners: kt:zh-measure-words-basic, kt:zh-lex-measure-extended, kt:ja-counters, kt:en-countability, kt:en-much-many, kt:en-fewer-less, kt:en-some-any, kt:en-determiners-wider, and errors like *a water in kt:en-articles-a-an
commonErrors include "omitting the classifier", "overusing 个", "assigning by Japanese counters", "matching by Chinese classifiers", "adding -s or a to an uncountable noun"
itemTypes include recognize-choice and situated-production-*
learnerSignals: Uses "个" or "つ" for everything
Pauses when counting, not knowing which word to put
In Japanese ordering says 三つのりんごをください
In English uses How many / How much at random, and puts -s on uncountable nouns
contraindications: Do not do it when the nouns themselves are not yet known
Do not judge "个" as an error: in most cases "个" is understood and is marked only as not idiomatic enough
Classifiers with large regional or personal variation (一颗苹果 / 一个苹果) are not used for forced-choice items

rules: Every line in Step 3 must contain a number, a classifier and a noun in the right order, and missing any one does not count (blocks an answer that is too weak)
If the general classifier (个, つ) makes up more than 60% of the whole list while the table has items with specific classifiers, mark it as "avoiding" (blocks gaming)
At least one quarter of the items in Step 2 are outside the shape pattern, and someone who chooses only by shape fails
Japanese sound items are judged by the complete reading, and an error in any of っ, voiced or semi-voiced sounds makes it wrong

English items: the determiner must agree with the box. many / a few / fewer may follow only items put in the "count directly" box, and much / a little / less only items in "cannot count directly". Each round has equal numbers of the two kinds of items, and someone who knows only one kind fails. Countable uses in ordering contexts such as a coffee and two waters are judged acceptable
check.independence: The box in which each item was first placed in Steps 1 and 2 is saved. A change after seeing the feature-label hint or "more commonly said …" is recorded as after hint. Step 3 does not show the box assignment of the items on the table

evidence.retained: Kept on the item table: the box in which each item was first placed, changes, the choice of the box feature labels; the list and connecting lines in Step 3; the proportion of general classifiers used

licensed.claim: can choose the classifier or countability marking for this set of common nouns
knows the class pattern behind this set of classifiers and its exceptions
actively uses specific classifiers in a task instead of always using 个

prohibited: Inferring that the learner can read the sound changes of Japanese counters from correct drag and drop
Inferring that the learner will also choose correctly for new nouns from correct items on the table
Judging that the learner does not know classifiers because they use 个

hints: Only ask "is it flat, long, or in pairs?"
Highlight an item already in the same box for comparison
Show the classifier usually used for this item directly (recorded as after hint)
scaffold.fade: After the first placement is right for 8 new items in a row under the same set of classifiers, the feature labels on the boxes are hidden by default. After 5 Japanese sound items in a row are all right at the first attempt, the sound-change coloring is no longer shown

primitives.reverseHalf: Classifiers do not all go by shape: 一把伞 (by handle), 一条新闻, 一场雨 (not shape but event). Japanese 本 is also used for phone calls, films and home runs. Sometimes both classifiers are right but the tone differs (一个人 / 一位老师). In English the countability of the same word changes with meaning (a coffee is a cup, coffee is the drink itself), so do not over-correct

failureModes.failure: The learner maps directly from the classifiers of Chinese or Japanese as the first language
failureModes.mitigation: Include items that the two languages assign differently (本, 枚, 张, 瓶)
failureModes.test: Adversarial example: 笔, 纸, 伞, 啤酒, 领带 appear in the same round

failureModes.failure: The learner uses 个 for everything and the list still "makes sense"
failureModes.mitigation: A usage-proportion check, and place items in the task that must be told apart (two pairs of shoes and two single shoes)
failureModes.test: Simulate an answer that uses 个 throughout, and check that it is marked as avoiding

failureModes.failure: The picture shape misleads (the table looks long)
failureModes.mitigation: Pictures use a uniform angle, and exception items are explicitly listed in Step 2 as outside the pattern
failureModes.test: Check the distribution of choices when table, bed and ticket appear together

stacksWith.how: The ordering sentences of Step 3 go onto the word-order track, and the difference in position between Japanese N を quantity V and Chinese number + classifier + noun is shown on the same sentence
The same items appear on a real menu or receipt, and the matching quantities and classifiers are found on the document
In the child variant, hearing a customer say "两双袜子" and dragging the items into the basket, the action itself is evidence of understanding
Sound changes in Japanese counters and the reading of large numbers are handled on the same list: first read the number right, then attach the counter

languages.en: Targets: judging countable versus uncountable, and the determination methods that go with it: a/an versus the zero article, plural -s, much / many, a few / a little, fewer / less, some / any followed by a plural countable or an uncountable, and container and unit phrases (a cup of, a piece of, a loaf of, a slice of). Material comes from kt:en-countability, kt:en-much-many, kt:en-fewer-less, kt:en-some-any, kt:en-determiners-wider. Traps: *an advice, *informations, *How many money, *a little apples, *less people. a coffee and two waters can be said in ordering contexts. less people is common in speech but regarded as an error in formal writing
languages.ja: Targets: つ・人・枚・本・個・台・冊・杯・匹, the sound changes around 1, 3, 6, 8, 10 (いっぽん・さんぼん・ろっぽん・はっぴき) and ひとり・ふたり. Word order N を quantity V. Material comes from kt:ja-counters. Trap: Chinese learners map 一瓶 onto 瓶, and treat 本 as books
languages.zh: Targets: 个, 本, 张, 杯, 口, 件, 条, 双, 套, 场, 顿, with the verbal measure words 次, 遍, 趟 as a separate group. Material comes from kt:zh-measure-words-basic, kt:zh-lex-measure-extended. Traps: English native speakers omit the classifier or use 个 for everything, and Japanese native speakers say "一本笔" and "一枚纸". Chinese heritage children mostly use 个 in speech, and writing asks for finer distinctions

primitives.name: Context guessing & look-up triage
primitives.oneLine: Mark the words that block reading, decide whether to look up or skip, and guess then revise the meaning over several encounters
primitives.difficulty: The learner goes wrong in both directions. Either they look up every unknown word, forget it right after, and read slowly and wearily; or they are told to "guess from context" without knowing where to look, and guess at random. They cannot tell which unknown words must be looked up and which can be skipped, and do not know when to stop guessing. The learner says "I can't understand it" but cannot say where.
primitives.object: A real short text slightly too hard for the learner (80 words or characters or more), with the blocking words already marked. Of these, 2–5 target unknown words each appear three times in the text, and each guess is kept on that word's card and may not be deleted
primitives.requires: Text coverage is roughly enough (the marked blocking words are no more than 18% of the whole text). If it is higher, do not fall back to another primitive; change to an easier text
learnerAction: Step 1 Triage: tap each blocking word and choose what kind of block it is (locked: do not know it / know it but it makes no sense here / cannot understand the phrase / it is a name). The coverage is calculated live on the right. Then judge each one as must look up or can skip (locked: must look up / will appear again later / the context gives the meaning / only an example / it is just a name)

Step 2 Three encounters: meet the same word three times. The first time you can only bet on one meaning, and the second and third times you revise it step by step as sentences unlock. Candidates already ruled out can no longer be chosen. For a word that is still not forced out after three times, that kind of word should be looked up

Step 3 Leave a clue: reverse the task and write a sentence so that someone who does not know a certain word can guess it after reading, and it must use one locked type of clue (giving a definition / saying it from the other side / giving an example / cause and effect)
systemResponse: After classification the word is colored by class, the background of the sentence it is in deepens by one layer, and the coverage gauge jumps. After the words that can be skipped have been judged, a second number appears: the coverage "after removing the ones that can be skipped"
After each encounter, the learner's own guess stays on the word's timeline. A candidate that has been ruled out is crossed out, with a mark showing which sentence ruled it out
For words that cannot be guessed, after three encounters the stopping condition is shown: when the same word is met a third time and two or more candidates remain, look it up

ui.screen: On the left is the original text, with blocking words carrying a dotted underline. On the upper right is the coverage gauge, and below it the three-encounter timeline for the current word (earlier guesses stay visible). Step 3 changes to a writing box and the choice of clue type
interactions: Tap a word, or use Tab to go through the blocking words, and number keys choose the class
In Step 2, for each encounter use number keys to bet on a candidate, and press "next encounter" to unlock the next sentence
The dictionary button is available only after the third encounter (except for words that cannot be guessed)
ui.childVariant: A short illustrated story, with one target word appearing three times and the candidates shown as pictures. No coverage or triage. Step 3 becomes saying aloud "which sentence I guessed it from"
ui.adultVariant: Material is taken from news, academic abstracts and manuals. Shows both coverage numbers and the clue terms. Step 3 writes two sentences
ui.accessibility: Class colors are paired with underline styles. Coverage is also shown as a number. Each guess on the timeline can be read out in order by a screen reader

kcSignals: component is strategic and the label involves guessing words from context, guessing from characters or morphemes, skimming and scanning (such as kt:en-str-guess-from-context, kt:en-str-dictionary-learning, kt:ja-str-guess-kanji, kt:zh-str-guess-morphemes)
itemTypes include read-comprehend
commonErrors include "looking up every word in the dictionary", "understanding by the literal meaning"
learnerSignals: Looks up a dozen words in one article
Does not know whether to look up or skip
Can only look up, cannot guess
"How do I guess a word from context?"
contraindications: More than 18% of the words in the text block reading: change the material
The target word appears only once in the text and there is no clue at all
In an exam situation that requires exact word meaning, the word-guessing strategy does not apply

rules: Material check: "will appear again later" holds only if the word really appears two or more times in the original; "the context gives the meaning" holds only if that sentence really has a definition marker; "it is a name" must be consistent across the two steps. The reason for skipping cannot be just talk, otherwise what is taught is a fake strategy

Material check: each target word has exactly three encounters; the first gives no clue and keeps all the candidates; candidates only decrease, never increase; a guessable word converges to exactly one at the end; at least one word is unguessable
Material check: at least two blocking words are marked as not worth remembering and at least two as must look up, so both false rules are blocked

Step 3: the sentence must contain the target word and must contain a marker word of the chosen clue type (blocks an answer that is too weak). The explanation after the marker word must be written in the target language and must not be a direct first-language translation (blocks gaming)
check.independence: The guess at each encounter is locked before the next sentence is unlocked and cannot be changed afterwards. Looking up the dictionary is recorded as "after look-up". The first bet in Step 2 and the first choice in the clue judgment are recorded separately

evidence.retained: For each word, the sequence of three guesses, the candidates ruled out and the sentence that ruled them out, the triage result and the two coverage numbers, and the sentence made in Step 3

licensed.claim: can use one class of clue in the text to revise a guess about word meaning
can tell which unknown words are worth looking up

prohibited: Treating a correct guess as remembering or mastering the word
Using the coverage number to infer how much was understood
Generalizing the triage result of one text to all genres
Treating looking up the dictionary as failure

hints: Don't look it up yet, bet on one, and it is fine if all four make sense
Highlight the clue marker word in this sentence
Show which class of clue this sentence gives
scaffold.fade: After two words in a row converge correctly at the second encounter, stop highlighting marker words

primitives.reverseHalf: Some words cannot be guessed even after three times (polysemy, a context that gives no clue), and then they should be looked up: guessing saves time, and holding on when it is time to look up makes things slower. A blocking word is not the same as a word worth remembering: names and over-narrow technical words are recognized and skipped. Conversely, not all unknown words can be skipped: every text has at least two must-look-up words, otherwise the learner will conclude "unknown words can all be skipped", a more dangerous false rule.

failureModes.failure: The learner looks up the dictionary at the first encounter, and the three encounters lose their meaning
failureModes.mitigation: The dictionary button unlocks only after the third encounter
failureModes.test: At the first encounter the dictionary button cannot be tapped

failureModes.failure: Clues are judged mechanically by marker word, for example treating every or as a choice
failureModes.mitigation: Put in the material both sentences where or means "that is" and sentences where or means a choice
failureModes.test: The adversarial examples include at least one sentence of each kind of or

failureModes.failure: Same-form kanji let a Japanese learner "guess right" the first time, when it is actually the wrong meaning
failureModes.mitigation: Japanese material specifically picks same-form-different-meaning kanji words as target words
failureModes.test: At least one of 大家, 留守, 迷惑 is a target word, and the first decoy is the Chinese meaning

stacksWith.how: At the first encounter, cut the unknown word, and use the meaning from the split as the candidate for the first bet
When judging "must look up", find the trunk first: only a word that is on the trunk and whose deletion makes the sentence collapse must be looked up
The words worth remembering left behind in Step 3 enter the recall cards a few days later

languages.en: The four block classes unknown/sense/chunk/name and the five dispositions must/later/defined/example/name are locked (c26); the four clue types define/contrast/example/cause plus none are locked (c27). Marker words: that is, or, a dash, a colon, unlike, such as, because. The surface marker of name is a capital initial, and of chunk is a space in the middle. The most valuable one is or meaning "that is". Existing implementations c26, c27
languages.ja: The block classes change to: do not know it; know the kanji but the meaning here is different (大家, 留守; Chinese learners should have no fewer than 3 in this class); cannot read it (knows the meaning of the character but cannot read it, a class of its own); it is a name (the surface marker changes to katakana personal or place names or proper nouns, since Japanese has no capital letters). The phrase class changes to idiomatic expressions (気がする, 手を焼く). Clue marker words: つまり, すなわち, a note in brackets, 〜ではなく, 一方, たとえば, 〜など, 〜ので, 〜ため, その結果
languages.zh: The learners are English native speakers. Chinese has no spaces, so in Step 1 the learner first marks the word boundaries and then classifies. The block classes change to: a character not known; all characters known but the word not understood (东西, 马上); a pattern not understood (越来越, 好不容易); it is a name (no capital letters, so it can be recognized only by the surname-plus-given-name pattern and place suffixes such as 市, 省, 路). Clue marker words: 也就是, 即, 就是说, 不是…而是, 跟…不同, 比如, 像…一样, …等, 因为, 所以, 导致

primitives.name: Form-for-meaning input
primitives.oneLine: Give only meaning-judgment items that can be answered by this one form, so the learner has to look at the ending, particle or marker
primitives.difficulty: The learner skips the form when reading. In English, a sentence with yesterday gets no look at -ed, and one with every day gets no look at walks. In Japanese, the learner does not check whether the ending is た, ている or ない, and treats を, に and が as optional. English-speaking learners reading Chinese ignore 了, 过, 着 and 在 and read the sentence by English tense (taking 了 as past tense). As long as the meaning can be guessed from context, the learner never looks at the form. Explaining the rule a hundred times does not help, because the learner has never been forced to judge meaning from this form alone.
primitives.object: A set of 6–12 sentences with every cue that could bypass the target form (time words, frequency words, context hints) removed. The judgments and the count of "shortcuts taken" stay on the same board
primitives.requires: Knows the content words in the sentences. Can use the first language to state the difference between the two meanings to be judged. Does not need to be able to produce the form. If the content words are unknown, change the material
learnerAction: Step 1 Judge meaning only: one target-language sentence with no time word, and two meaning options written in the first language (He is still in Nanjing / He is no longer in Nanjing). Only the form decides the answer. After a wrong choice, mark which shortcut the learner nearly fell into and give one pointer without revealing the answer. The learner can choose again

Step 2 About you: one sentence about "me". The learner picks "Same for me / Not the same for me". There is no right or wrong. After the choice, show what this form says, and what the meaning becomes if the form is swapped

Step 3 Two sentences, one small difference: two situations and one target-language sentence. The learner decides which situation it belongs to. The two sentences differ only in this one form, and both are grammatical. This primitive deliberately has no production step
systemResponse: Correct: say what the form does here, then add one thing to remember along the way
Wrong: add one to the matching count in the "shortcuts" list on the right, and give one pointer (without the answer). The learner can choose again

After Step 2, show the original sentence and the sentence with the form swapped side by side, with the changed form coloured and the change in meaning written below. The closing page says what this round practised and which primitive to use for practising production

ui.screen: A sentence card in the middle with two large buttons (the meaning options) below it. A column on the right lists the locked shortcuts, each with its own count. Shortcuts not tested in this set are marked "Not tested this time". No accuracy rate is shown
interactions: Left and right arrow keys, or 1 and 2, to choose
Enter to go to the next item
Step 2 "Same for me / Not the same for me" uses the same two keys
ui.childVariant: The two options become two pictures (the cat is chasing the dog / the dog is chasing the cat; is eating / has finished eating). The sentence is read aloud. 6 items per set
ui.adultVariant: Sentences come from news and work email. The closing page shows the grammar terms and the name of the rule
ui.accessibility: The two option buttons are the same size and colour, in fixed positions. Sentences can be read aloud. The target form is underlined only at the hint stage, not otherwise

kcSignals: component is grammatical, the form is an ending, particle or marker, and it carries aspect-*, time-*, reference-person or agent-patient relations (e.g. kt:en-past-simple, kt:en-third-person-s, kt:en-passive-simple, kt:ja-result-state-teiru, kt:ja-passive-person, kt:ja-case-particles, kt:zh-le-perfective, kt:zh-guo-experience, kt:zh-zhe-durative, kt:zh-ba-sentence)
commonErrors contain form-bypassing errors such as "relies on a time word to express the past" or "treats 了 as past tense"
itemTypes include recognize-choice and read-comprehend
learnerSignals: skips word endings when reading
understands the form but does not look at it while reading
can recite the grammar rule but cannot use it when reading
reads passive sentences backwards
contraindications: the form does not carry a difference in meaning in this context (both forms work and mean the same)
the learner can already judge reliably from the form and needs production; switch to prim:choose-by-intent
