Describe each card as a single picture first, then string them into a retelling
When listening to a story, bet on the next card between each pair of cards first, then reveal and check

languages.en: Linking devices first/then/after that/finally, when/while/before/after; tense and aspect simple past and past perfect (When I arrived, she had left); traps *Then the rabbit see a carrot, listing events with no background and no ending; the reading direction of c35-tense-shifts can serve as input material
languages.ja: Linking devices Vてから, Vて, Vて、それから, その後, 最後に, Vる前に／Vた後で, ～ていた (background); traps: 前に takes the dictionary form and 後で takes the た form; keep the narrative register consistent from start to end (です・ます or だ)
languages.zh: Linking devices 先……再……, 然后, 最后, ……以前／以后 (placed after the clause); narration uses 了, and flashback uses 之前已经……了; traps *昨天我先吃饭，再看电影, *以后下课, *在吃饭以后, always using 然后

primitives.name: Grow a text
primitives.oneLine: Starting from one sentence, expand it step by step into a paragraph following prompts, with every step staying on the same text
primitives.difficulty: A paragraph gets two sentences and then nothing more to say. To reach the word count, learners invent data, restate the claim in other words, or write "studies show" with no source. When describing change they know only "rises / falls", and degree, time span and comparison are all missing. What learners lack is the choice of "which direction to grow in", and the judgment that "this direction is empty this time".
primitives.object: One bare claim (or a line graph with four to six segments of trend). The whole process grows on the same text, and every piece keeps a record of how it grew.
primitives.requires: The learner can write a correct sentence stating the claim itself and knows the most basic linking devices. If even single sentences cannot be written correctly, fall back and build sentences first.
learnerAction: Step 1 Choose a way to grow: choose one way to grow (give an example / give a number / state the opposite / tell the consequence; in the change-description version: direction / degree / time span / comparison), and from three candidate sentences pick the one that really moves the paragraph forward. For one of the ways of growing this sentence has nothing to give, and the learner must press "nothing to add on this one" (the reverse half).
Step 2 Recognise the opening formulas: several items share the same set of opening formulas, and the learner judges which one each place should use.
Step 3 Grow a paragraph yourself: with a new claim (or a new set of data), grow it into a paragraph on your own.
systemResponse: When the right sentence is chosen, the paragraph grows by one piece, the word-count progress bar rises (8 → 29 → 47 → 62), and this piece takes on a label for the way of growing.
When a padding candidate is picked, it does not enter the paragraph, and the system shows why it is padding (made-up number / no number at all / the claim restated).
In the change-description version, word cards are attached by leader lines to a segment of the line graph. A segment that nothing can be attached to shows "this segment is not worth writing about".
After Step 3 is submitted, each piece is marked with the way of growing it belongs to, and the missing ways and the blocked padding sentences are marked separately.

ui.screen: Above is the paragraph being grown (each piece with a label for its way of growing). Below are the buttons for the ways of growing and the three candidate sentences. On the right is the word-count progress bar. In the change-description version the top is replaced by a line graph.
interactions: Number keys choose the way of growing, arrow keys move between candidate sentences, and Enter confirms
Change-description version: first select a word card, then click a line segment
Step 3 is typed, and opening formulas can be clicked to insert (inserting counts as a hint)
ui.childVariant: Three question buttons, "For example?", "And then?" and "So?", replace the terms, growing from one sentence to three or four sentences. It can be spoken with an adult taking notes. The change-description version uses a height chart or a bean-sprout growth picture.
ui.adultVariant: Opinion paragraphs, chart descriptions in reports, weekly work updates. Terms for the ways of growing and the opening formulas are shown. Step 3 must grow to at least four times the starting length.
ui.accessibility: The progress bar comes with the number. The line graph has a data-table alternative. Labels for the ways of growing are presented in text.

kcSignals: itemTypes include situated-production-written
component is discourse or activity (writing paragraphs, describing charts, summarising), such as kt:ja-skill-write-paragraph
the label contains 段落／描述变化／趋势／paragraph
learnerSignals: "I have nothing to say after two sentences"
essays do not reach the word count
"how do I develop it"
can only describe a chart as rising or falling
contraindications: single sentences are still not written correctly
when the task itself requires brevity (notices, text messages), use the cutting version of prim:one-fix-revision instead
when the learner really has no usable examples or data, do not force them to "give a number"

rules: Step 3: must grow to more than four times the starting length, and use at least three ways of growing (blocks an answer that is too weak).

Made-up percentages and "studies show" with no source (en Studies show / ja 研究によると / zh 据研究) must not appear, and a "consequence" sentence that largely overlaps the original claim does not count (blocks padding).
The opening formulas taught in Step 2 must be recognised in Step 3: writing as taught cannot be judged as failing.
The candidate sentence for the empty way of growing in Step 1 must be catchable by the no-invented-numbers rule in Step 3.
check.independence: The first choice each time in Step 1 is recorded separately. Step 3 does not show candidate sentences, only the names of the ways of growing. Clicking to insert an opening formula is recorded as completed after a hint.

evidence.retained: Each piece of the paragraph and its label for the way of growing, the rejected padding candidates, and the Step 3 paragraph are all kept on the same text.

licensed.claim: Can tell expanding sentences that move the paragraph forward from padding sentences
Can independently expand one claim into a structurally complete paragraph
Can expand in a given direction in two or more genres (opinion paragraph, change description)

prohibited: Inferring writing quality from growth in word count
Inferring quality of argument from correct use of opening formulas
Treating a rewrite after an invented number is blocked as evidence that the learner already has the awareness

hints: Ask only: "For example? What would happen then? How would the other side object?"
Give the opening formula for that way of growing
Give one candidate sentence and let the learner judge whether it moves forward or is padding
scaffold.fade: After two consecutive Step 3 runs use all three ways of growing without looking at hints, the opening-formula button is no longer shown.

primitives.reverseHalf: For one way of growing, this sentence has nothing to give: with no number at hand, do not give a number, because an invented number does more harm than writing none. In a change description one segment is noise and not worth writing about. Not every direction can always be added to.

failureModes.failure: To "give a number", the learner invents a percentage
failureModes.mitigation: The no-invented-numbers rule catches percentages and sources-free research
failureModes.test: "Studies show that 87%…" and "据研究，87%……" must be blocked

failureModes.failure: The original claim is restated in other words and passed off as a consequence
failureModes.mitigation: Check the overlap between the consequence sentence and the claim
failureModes.test: A simulated answer of In conclusion／总之 + the original sentence does not count as "tell the consequence"

failureModes.failure: Opening formulas are piled up but the content is empty
failureModes.mitigation: An example sentence must contain a specific noun, and a number sentence must have a source or a range
failureModes.test: "比如，有很多例子。" does not count as an example

failureModes.failure: The learner writes with the opening formulas taught but is judged as failing
failureModes.mitigation: All opening formulas in Step 2 are included in what Step 3 recognises
failureModes.test: Writing one sentence with each taught opening formula must pass

stacksWith.how: The paragraph grown in Step 3 is sealed as the first draft and then compared with a model sentence by sentence
The growth-way label on each piece is its function label in the discourse, and the same paragraph goes straight into the judgment of discourse shape
In the change-description version, every number must carry a unit or time span, checked with the same two-cell check

languages.en: Locked ways of growing eg / num / against / so, opening formulas Take …, for instance / In the first year alone, / The obvious objection is that / Which means that; four kinds of words for describing change: verbs (rose / fell / levelled off), degree (sharply / slightly), time span (between September and November), comparison (three times as many). Existing implementations c38, c46
languages.ja: Opening formulas: たとえば～ / ～だけでも (giving a number) / もちろん～という意見もある。しかし～ (stating the opposite) / そのため～・つまり～ (telling the consequence); change description: 増える・減る・横ばい, 大幅に・わずかに, ～から～にかけて, ～倍. Note the register should be consistent across the whole paragraph, and an unsourced "研究によると" is banned.
languages.zh: Opening formulas: 比如说…… / 光是第一年就…… / 有人会说……，但是…… / 这样一来……; change description: 上升／下降／持平, 大幅／略微／逐渐, 从……到……, 是原来的三倍 (the ambiguity between "增加了两倍" and "增加到两倍" is a trap); ban "据研究" and "众所周知"; intermediate learners should note paired connectives.

primitives.name: Carry across
primitives.oneLine: Move expressions already learned onto a matter of your own that has nothing to do with the original material, and check which parts can move and which must change
primitives.difficulty: Between understanding an expression and being able to use it lies a move: of the hundreds of "learned" expressions in the notes, not one can be called up, because they have never left the sentence where they first appeared. The other extreme is moving things wildly: forcing an expression tied to its original setting into a setting where that thing does not exist, or carrying meeting-speak to the dinner table.
primitives.object: A set of expressions highlighted from the original material (a recording or a text), and a matter of the learner's own that has nothing to do with the original material. The expressions are moved from the original words on the left into the learner's own matter on the right.
primitives.requires: The learner has already understood these expressions in the original material by listening or reading. If not yet understood, fall back to collecting and trying them out first.
learnerAction: Step 1 Cross the bridge: the expressions in the original words on the left are highlighted, the learner's own matter on the right is left blank, and the learner moves the expressions across, keeping them as they are when they should be kept and changing words when they should change.

Step 2 Judge how far it moves: judge for each expression how far it can move (locked options: move directly / swap the words inside / move only the first half / can move but the tone must change / cannot move — the reverse half).
Step 3 Tell about something completely unrelated: using at least three expressions, tell about one matter of your own, and do not bring across anything from the original setting.
systemResponse: After the move, the frame kept and the content replaced in the sentence on the right are shown with two kinds of marking.
When an expression that cannot move is dragged over, it bounces back and the system shows that the thing it needs does not exist in the new setting.
After classification, the "content part" and the "frame part" of that expression in the original words are marked separately.
After Step 3 is submitted, the expressions used are marked one by one, and nouns brought over from the original setting are marked "this is his matter".

ui.screen: On the left is the original-words card (expressions highlighted), on the right is the card for the learner's own matter (empty slots), with a bridge in between. Step 2 has five category buttons. Step 3 is a text box, with a side list of expressions that can be ticked.
interactions: Drag an expression across the bridge, or select it and press Enter
Number keys 1–5 classify
Step 3 is typed or recorded inside the page
ui.childVariant: The original material is one sentence from a story ("Can I … ?" "It's my turn"), and the new setting is the child's own home or school. Only two categories, "can move / cannot move", and it is spoken.
ui.adultVariant: Expressions from meetings, podcasts and news are moved into the learner's own work and life. Register adjustment is allowed, and categories are shown with terms.
ui.accessibility: Dragging has a keyboard alternative. The "this is his matter" mark uses both an icon and text. Frame and content are not distinguished by colour alone.

kcSignals: mastery is written at the "use in context" level
itemTypes include situated-production-spoken or situated-production-written
component is functional or lexical (chunks, fixed expressions, spoken patterns, such as kt:zh-colloquial-formats)
learnerSignals: "I've learned it, but I just can't use it"
when expressing themselves can only repeat the original text
in essays copies textbook sentences as they are, along with their setting
contraindications: the expression itself is not yet understood
the expression is a proper noun or term, which does not transfer anyway
when the learner has no matter of their own to tell about (such as young children), use an imagined role instead

rules: Step 3: at least three different expressions, of which at least one belongs to the "swap words" or "half" type (blocks an answer that is too weak and against picking only the easiest).
Nouns from the original setting must not appear (blocks copying).

Each expression's model move must pass its own judging rule; the judging rule must not be so loose that an empty string passes; for the "move directly" type, the original expression itself must be accepted.
Exactly one expression cannot move, and the explanation states clearly which thing in the new setting it lacks.
check.independence: The first way each expression is moved in Step 1 is recorded separately. Step 3 does not show model moves; ticking the expression list does not count as a hint, and opening a model counts as completed after a hint.

evidence.retained: The way each expression was moved, its classification, the first and revised versions, and the expressions hit in the Step 3 text are all kept on this set of expression cards.

licensed.claim: Can judge whether an expression can leave its original setting
Can actively use newly learned expressions in an unrelated topic
These expressions have entered transferable, active production

prohibited: Inferring from one use in Step 3 that an expression has entered long-term production (supported requires independent use in at least three topics and at two or more different times)
Counting repeating as is as transfer
Judging quality of expression by the number of expressions used

hints: Ask only: "If you take the nouns out of this expression, what is left?"
Mark the frame part and the content part of the expression in two colours
Give a model move
scaffold.fade: Once an expression has been used correctly and independently in two different topics, it no longer appears in the hint list and stays only in the learner's own chunk book.

primitives.reverseHalf: One expression cannot move: it is tied to something that does not exist at all in the new setting (a committee, an approval process), and once the specific content is removed nothing is left. Another type can move but the tone is wrong: meeting-speak carried to the dinner table will make the other person think you are joking.

failureModes.failure: The judging rule is too strict, and writing according to the model is judged wrong
failureModes.mitigation: Run every model through its own judging rule
failureModes.test: All model moves can pass

failureModes.failure: The learner carries the original setting's nouns along with the expression
failureModes.mitigation: The banned-word list is taken from the nouns in the original words
failureModes.test: An original-words noun appearing in Step 3 is blocked

failureModes.failure: The learner picks only empty "move directly" frames to make up the number
failureModes.mitigation: Require at least one swap-word or half type
failureModes.test: A simulated answer using only three move-directly expressions does not pass

failureModes.failure: The new topic in Step 3 is in fact close to the original material, so no move takes place
failureModes.mitigation: When setting items, check the keyword overlap between the new topic and the original material
failureModes.test: An item is rejected when the keyword overlap between old and new topics exceeds two

stacksWith.how: The expressions collected in the chunk book directly become the highlights on the left, and the results of the move are written back to the same chunk book
When an expression that "needs a different tone" crosses the bridge, the relationship sliders open and are set to the level of the new setting on the same sentence
The Step 3 text is saved as the first draft for the next piece of writing

languages.en: Five locked types free / swap / half / tone / stuck, for example In other words (move directly), spread over three years (swap words), It goes to the committee (cannot move); common for Chinese native speakers: memorising the expression together with the nouns of its original setting; existing implementation c57
languages.ja: Frames suited to moving: ～ということになっています, ～わけではない, ～てみたらどうですか, 正直に言うと～. There are many "tone must change" cases in particular: ～と存じます in a meeting must become ～と思う among friends, and when moving, the register must be unified with the new setting. Cannot move: expressions tied to organisational procedures (稟議に回す).
languages.zh: Frames suited to moving: 说白了……, ……也好，……也好, 问题是……, 跟……比起来. "Tone must change" cases: written or news register (据悉, 予以) moved to chat must become colloquial. Cannot move: expressions tied to institutions (报批, 走流程) placed in a family setting. When moving four-character phrases, mind the collocation (*非常地五花八门).

primitives.name: Real-document scanning
primitives.oneLine: On real documents such as menus, timetables, notices and forms, find the one entry needed to complete the task
primitives.difficulty: Faced with a real document (menu, timetable, notice, form, announcement, bill), learners translate word by word from the top and cannot find the one entry needed to complete the task. They misread format conventions: the 24-hour clock versus a.m./p.m.; No smoking understood as "there is none"; missing the prohibition in ～ないでください; 入口 read as 人口; 大家 understood as "everyone" (in Japanese it means the landlord); missing exceptions in footnotes (土休日運休, ※要予約).
primitives.object: A real or realistic document that keeps its original layout, paired with a concrete task ("catch a bus that gets to the airport before ten", "order a dish with no peanuts for under 2,000 yen", "find what this notice forbids"). Locating, extracting information and completing the product all happen on this document.
primitives.requires: The learner knows the types of key information the task needs (numbers, times, prices) and the core words of this kind of document. If not, first go through prim:scene-walkthrough.
learnerAction: Step 1 Locate first: do not read line by line, but first choose which kind of information is wanted and in which zone of the layout (header, a column, footnote, icon), and frame that area on the document. The first framing is saved.

Step 2 Extract the information and judge the conditions: within the frame, click the entry that is the answer, then judge each condition of the task: applies / does not apply / has an exception (footnote, weekdays only, ※) / cannot be found on the document (the last is the reverse half: for some tasks the document has no answer, and the right thing to do is to ask).
Step 3 Use it: use the information found to complete the task product: fill in a form, write a message to a friend ("We'll take the 9:40 bus"), place an order.
systemResponse: After framing, the area outside the frame fades, and the areas the learner has viewed are recorded in order as a scanning path.
After the answer is clicked, the conditions of the task are checked one by one, and any one not met is marked (the time is right, but the service does not run that day because it is a weekend).
When a footnote symbol is clicked, the view links automatically to the footnote line. When "cannot be found" is chosen, an entry is shown for whom to ask and how (connecting to prim:info-gap).

ui.screen: The document takes the main area, can be zoomed and panned, and keeps its original layout. The task card is fixed at the top. On the right are the "What I found" slots and a row of condition-judgment buttons.
interactions: Drag to frame an area, or use the keyboard arrow keys to move the selection and Shift to extend it
Click an entry to put it in a slot, and number keys choose the condition judgment
Pinch to zoom; zooming does not disturb the layout
ui.childVariant: Picture-and-text menus, timetables, park notices, theme-park maps. The task is to point to one icon or one time. The condition judgment has only two options, "allowed / not allowed".
ui.adultVariant: Real-layout train timetables, flat-rental notices, hospital registration slips, electricity bills, sign-up forms. The task contains two or three conditions and one footnote exception. The Step 3 product is a message to be sent or a completed form.
ui.accessibility: A text version with table semantics is provided separately for screen readers, but completing with the text version is recorded as a different task condition. Zooming does not lose the layout. No reliance on colour.

kcSignals: the KC is reading informational material or filling in forms (kt:en-skill-read-informational, kt:en-skill-read-signs, kt:en-skill-write-forms, kt:en-str-skim-scan, kt:en-skill-read-documents, kt:ja-skill-read-daily, kt:ja-skill-write-forms-memo, kt:ja-fn-schedule, kt:ja-fn-transport, kt:zh-skill-read-basic, kt:zh-skill-write-basic)
itemTypes include read-comprehend and match
commonErrors include misreading of format conventions (24-hour clock, No + V-ing, look-alike characters, transfer of kanji-word meanings)
learnerSignals: reads a menu word by word with a dictionary
"I know all the words but I just can't find it"
cannot read the timetable before a trip
contraindications: the document contains many typefaces or handwriting not yet learned, far beyond the learner's level
the task requires close reading of the meaning of clauses (contract liability), in which case use prim:strip-skeleton or prim:source-stance
do not ask learners to upload their own real bills or identity documents

rules: The answer entry is correct and satisfies all the conditions of the task (time, price, exceptions) (blocks an answer that is too weak).

The first framing must contain the answer and cover no more than one third of the layout. A scanning path that frames the whole page, or clicks through all entries line by line, is judged "not scanned" (blocks gaming).

The task card uses paraphrase rather than the document's own words, so keyword matching alone cannot locate the answer. For "cannot be found" tasks, the learner must choose "not on the document" and write what to do next.
check.independence: The first framing and the first answer are recorded separately. Completion after using an area hint or an explanation of a format convention is recorded as assisted. Completion with the text version is recorded separately.

evidence.retained: The scanning path (the areas viewed and their order), the first framing, the answer entry, the condition judgments, and the completed product.

licensed.claim: Can locate the information the task needs in this type of document
Can handle conditions and exceptions in a document

prohibited: Inferring that the whole text was understood from finding the information
Inferring performance in a real environment from performance on a realistic document
Scoring the scanning path itself as reading ability

hints: Ask only: "Where in the layout is this kind of information usually found?"
Highlight the relevant area (the header or a column)
Explain one format convention (24-hour clock, ※, weekdays / weekends and holidays)
scaffold.fade: After two consecutive documents of the same type are hit on the first framing, the area hints are no longer offered.

primitives.reverseHalf: Scanning is not just finding keywords: for some tasks the document has no answer at all and one must ask someone; some entries that look like the answer are ruled out by a footnote or exception (土日祝運休, ※要予約, Sat only). Each set has at least one item of each kind.

failureModes.failure: The learner does only keyword matching
failureModes.mitigation: The task card is paraphrased and does not use the document's own words
failureModes.test: Adversarial example: first-attempt accuracy when the task card has zero vocabulary overlap with the document

failureModes.failure: The layout gives the answer away (the answer is always in bold or on the first line)
failureModes.mitigation: Choose documents whose answers sit in different positions
failureModes.test: Count the distribution of answer positions on the layouts

failureModes.failure: The learner translates the whole document, taking time but finally getting it right
failureModes.mitigation: Record the scanning path and require in Step 1 that the area be framed first
failureModes.test: Compare scanning-path length with accuracy to confirm the judgment does not look at the result alone

stacksWith.how: Lay an announcement over the same timetable: after hearing a change, amend that entry on the document
A word in the way is decided on the spot, look it up or skip it, and words looked up are noted in the margin of the same document
A task that cannot be found on the document is turned into a question to be asked, and the question itself is recorded

languages.en: Documents: menus, timetables, notices, forms. Traps: converting between the 24-hour clock and a.m./p.m., No + V-ing / No + noun meaning prohibition, Push/Pull and Entrance/Exit, Surname / First name, British and American date formats (05/06)
languages.ja: Documents: timetables (平日／土休日, 始発, 快速), notices, forms (フリガナ, 氏名, 〒), prices (税込／税抜), Japanese era years. Kanji-word traps 大家, 留守, 切手; missing ～ないでください
languages.zh: Documents: menus (often without pictures), opening hours, notices (禁止吸烟, 请勿……), forms (姓名, 身份证号, 联系电话). Traps: look-alike characters such as 入口／人口, 大／太, traditional and simplified forms; for Japanese native speakers, transfer of kanji-word meanings (走, 手纸)

primitives.name: Scale placement
primitives.oneLine: First place a set of forms on a ladder by certainty / obligation / degree / frequency, then choose a rung on the ladder according to the situation
primitives.difficulty: A set of forms expressing certainty, obligation or degree is often squashed into one or two words in the learner's mind ("maybe", "should", "very"), so the learner cannot see the difference in strength between them: in English, speculation is always maybe and requirement is always must; in Japanese, speculation is always かもしれない; in Chinese, degree is always "很". More hidden is the asymmetry of negation: must not and don't have to, てはいけない and なくてもいい, "一定不" and "不一定" are treated as stronger and weaker versions of the same meaning.
primitives.object: A vertical ladder (strong at the top, weak at the bottom) and a set of sentence cards that say the same thing and differ in only one form. From Step 2 a situation card is added, and the three things are always on the same screen.
primitives.requires: The learner can already recognise the form and basic meaning of each form on the ladder (see prim:form-for-meaning). If the forms are not recognised yet, go back first.
learnerAction: Step 1 Order the ladder: drag 4–5 sentence cards that differ in only one form onto the ladder, from the strongest to the weakest (speculation, obligation and degree are each a separate ladder and are not mixed).

Step 2 Fix a rung: given a situation (who the other person is, how certain the matter is, how important), click on the ladder the rung that should be said, and judge where the other rungs go wrong (locked options: too strong / too weak / moved to another ladder / either of two rungs would do here — the last is the reverse half, for example the speculative and obligation senses of must, "一定" for speculation and "一定要").

Step 3 Say it twice: say or write one matter of your own twice, the two versions must land at least one rung apart on the ladder, and for each version write one sentence "in what situation I would say it this way".
systemResponse: After the order is set, the ladder spreads out according to the true relative spacing: two adjacent rungs of similar strength sit close together, and those far apart are spread out, so the learner sees where their own order and spacing differ.

After a rung is chosen in Step 2, "how the other side will understand it: …" appears on the situation card. Too strong is shown as commanding or dogmatic, and too weak as "it's not important" or "you're not sure yourself", rather than just right or wrong.

In negation items, when the negation word on a sentence card is dragged to a different position, the landing point on the ladder moves or flips synchronously (不一定 lands in the middle, 一定不 lands at the opposite end of the top), so the learner sees which rung the position of the negation changes.

ui.screen: On the left is a vertical ladder (4–5 rungs, with a Chinese description of strength beside each rung such as "non-negotiable / most likely / hard to say / up to the other person"). On the right is the stack of sentence cards, and above is the situation card. At the bottom of the ladder is a distribution bar, "the rungs you chose in this set", with no score shown.
interactions: Drag sentence cards onto the ladder; with the keyboard use the up and down arrows to move a card and Enter to put it down
In Step 2 click a rung or press number keys 1–5 to choose
Step 3 is typed or recorded (the recording is played back only inside the page and not scored automatically)
ui.childVariant: The ladder becomes a volume knob or a thermometer picture ("how sure it sounds"), with only three rungs. Sentences are a picture scene with one line, such as "it will rain tomorrow" with three sky pictures (full of dark clouds / half cloudy / sunny). No terms appear.
ui.adultVariant: Situations are taken from emails, meetings, medical advice, news reports. Terms can be shown (epistemic / deontic, 確信度). Step 3 requires writing a "strong version" and a "weak version" of the same fact and explaining who each is used with.
ui.accessibility: Ladder rungs are distinguished by position, text and colour together. Every drag has a keyboard alternative. The screen reader reads "rung 3 of 5". On phones the ladder lies horizontally at the top, and the sentence cards below can be tapped and then a rung tapped to place them.

kcSignals: notions include possibility-probability, obligation, necessity, or include emphasis-focus with a KC about degree (such as kt:zh-degree-extreme)
the KC label is a set of parallel forms of the same kind (will / probably / may / might; 可能、大概、也许、一定; かもしれない／はずだ／にちがいない; 应该、得、必须、不用)
commonErrors include negation position or asymmetry of negation (*你不必须来, *他一定不来 meant as "not necessarily", must not / don't have to mixed up)
commonErrors mention register mismatch (using にちがいない in casual chat, writing "忙死了" in a formal email)
learnerSignals: emails are must／必须 all the way, or maybe／かもしれない all the way
reads an author's guess as a conclusion, or a conclusion as a guess
"Is it too blunt to say it this way?" "Have I said this too definitely?"
after being corrected once, softens everything to the weakest
contraindications: the learner cannot yet recognise or inflect the forms on the ladder
when the point of the KC is how the forms connect (such as how to attach *休みだかもしれない) rather than strength, first use prim:form-for-meaning or prim:paradigm-apply
when the difference between two rungs is mainly register rather than strength, use prim:register-calibrate instead

rules: In Step 3 both versions must contain forms on the ladder, and the two versions must land at least one rung apart (blocks an answer that is too weak: swapping a near-synonym on the same rung does not count).
Adding degree words or polite phrases to the sentence (very, とても, 麻烦您) without changing the form on the ladder does not count as changing rung (blocks gaming).
When 4 consecutive items in Step 2 choose the middle rung, prompt "you may be choosing the safest rung" and insert an item where the middle rung is clearly wrong.
A negation item passes only if the negation word is put in the right position (不一定 vs 一定不, don't have to vs must not).
check.independence: The first ordering in Step 1 is recorded separately, and an adjustment after seeing the ladder spread out is recorded as completed after a hint. A changed choice in Step 2 after seeing "how the other side will understand it" is recorded as after a hint. Step 3 shows no model sentences.

evidence.retained: The first and final ordering on each ladder, the first-choice and revised rung for each situation, the strong and weak versions in Step 3 and the learner's usage notes are all kept on this set of ladder cards.

licensed.claim: Can order the relative strength of this set of forms in controlled material
Can choose the suitable rung for the situation, neither too strong nor too weak
Can actively adjust the strength of what is said in own situations

prohibited: Judging that the learner can use the forms from correct ordering alone
Carrying performance on one ladder (such as speculation) over to another ladder (such as obligation)
Recording as mastery of strength cases where the learner always picks the middle rung and happens to be right
Judging the learner's personality or politeness from this

hints: Ask only: "How sure is the person saying this? Is this something that must be done, or can be done or not?"
Show beside the ladder the Chinese description of strength for each rung (most likely, hard to say …)
Give one minimal-contrast example sentence for each of two adjacent rungs, and mark how the other side understands them differently
scaffold.fade: After 4 consecutive situations on the same ladder are chosen correctly on the first attempt, remove the Chinese strength descriptions beside the rungs and leave an empty ladder.

primitives.reverseHalf: There is no best rung on the ladder: too soft is as wrong as too hard, and each set has at least one item whose correct answer is the top rung. A plain statement with nothing added is itself a strong assertion (The drug helps with sleep is bolder than Some researchers believe…). The same form can sit on two ladders (must be speculation / must do obligation; "一定" speculation / "一定要" obligation; "应该" can express speculation or obligation), and negation changes the landing point rather than simply lowering it by one rung.

failureModes.failure: The learner orders by sentence length or by the number of polite words
failureModes.mitigation: Make sure the longest sentence is not always the weakest, and add cards that are short and weak (might) and long and strong (I'm absolutely certain that…)
failureModes.test: The correlation between sentence length and strength in the adversarial examples is close to zero

failureModes.failure: A register difference is mistaken for a strength difference (にちがいない is just more written, "死了" is just colloquial)
failureModes.mitigation: Step 2 has dedicated items where "the strength is right but the register is wrong", with answers leading to prim:register-calibrate
failureModes.test: Include two situations where strength is correct and register is wrong, and check whether they are wrongly judged "too strong / too weak"

failureModes.failure: The learner memorises the ladder order and applies it mechanically without looking at the situation
failureModes.mitigation: Pair the same ladder with several situations, with the correct rungs spread across the ladder
failureModes.test: Check that the correct answers for each set of situations cover at least three rungs

stacksWith.how: On the same situation card, the ladder handles strength and the relationship labels handle politeness level; when the learner adjusts one rung they see at the same time whether both are suitable
Reading direction: in the same article, first order the certainty ladder, then point the basis of each rung back to its place in the original text
The strong and weak versions from Step 3 are saved as a first draft, and later checked again with the same check in an email or an essay

languages.en: Ladders: certainty will／must／probably／may／might／can't; obligation must／have to／should／don't have to／mustn't; past inference must have／might have／can't have. Existing implementations c34 (reading direction, the author's certainty) and c17 (writing direction, required strength) lack the matching separate ladders for the speculative and obligation senses and the flip under negation. Traps: must not versus don't have to, can't used for inference meaning "surely not"
languages.ja: Ladders: certainty かもしれない／だろう／はずだ／にちがいない; obligation なければならない／べきだ／たほうがいい／なくてもいい／てはいけない; はずがない is the reverse top rung of the certainty ladder. Traps: Chinese "可能" mistranslated as the potential form (*雨が降れる); にちがいない leans written, and using it in casual chat is a register problem rather than a strength problem
languages.zh: Ladders: speculation 也许／可能／大概／一定; obligation 不用／可以／应该／得 děi／必须; degree 有点儿／比较／很／非常／极了／死了; hedging 恐怕、好像、不一定. Traps: asymmetry of negation (*你不必须来 → 你不用来; "一定不" versus "不一定"), "有点儿" carrying a negative evaluation, "死了" used only in speech, "可能" does not equal can

primitives.name: Viewpoint & direction
primitives.oneLine: Fix where the speaker stands and who the action moves toward first, then choose the giving/receiving, coming/going or passive/causative form
primitives.difficulty: Chinese "给", "借" and "来/去" rarely force the speaker to mark where they stand, so learners pick a form without fixing the viewpoint first. In Japanese, a friend giving me something becomes *友達が私にあげました, and waiting at home becomes *早く帰っていってね. In English, lend/borrow are both "借", bring/take are both "拿", and I'm coming (to where you are) is said as I'm going. English-speaking learners of Chinese say *他从外面进去了 while the speaker is inside the room, or swap an English passive straight for "被". The learner is not missing words. The missing step is "where do I stand, and who is the thing moving toward?"
primitives.object: A top-down scene picture: two or three characters, two locations (home/school, inside/outside), a draggable "I am here" marker, and an arrow showing giving or movement. The same scene runs through all three steps.
primitives.requires: The learner already recognizes the basic shapes of the giving/receiving, coming/going or passive/causative forms. The words for the characters and places in the scene are already known. If the scene picture itself cannot be understood, fall back to prim:listen-and-do.
learnerAction: Step 1 Place yourself: read a situation description, put the "I" marker in the scene, draw the arrow (who gives to whom, which way the movement goes, who is affected), then choose the form

Step 2 Move the viewpoint: the event stays the same; move the "I" marker to another character or location and decide whether the form must change (locked options: it changes, because the arrow's direction relative to "I" is reversed / it does not change, because this form does not depend on the speaker's position / both are possible but the feeling differs. The last option is the reverse half, e.g. adversity passive vs. ordinary passive, てくれる vs. a neutral statement)
Step 3 Tell your own story: tell about something in your own life that you gave, received, moved or were affected by. First set "I" and the arrow on the scene picture, then say or write it
systemResponse: After the learner chooses a form, a line is drawn between the arrow and "I" and its direction is highlighted (toward me / away from me), showing that the form is decided by this direction
When the "I" marker is dragged, the sentence under the scene changes form in real time (あげる→くれる, go→come, take→bring), so the learner sees which single word changes with the viewpoint

If the learner chooses a form that does not match the arrow, it is not marked wrong. The system shows "Said this way, the listener will think you are standing at ..." and puts a shadow of the "I" marker at that position

ui.screen: The top-down scene is in the middle. The "I" marker is a prominent eye icon and the arrow has draggable endpoints. Below are a row of form buttons (2–4) and a sentence strip that changes with the viewpoint. A narrow right column records which viewpoints have been used in this set.
interactions: Drag the "I" marker and the arrow endpoints; by keyboard, Tab selects a character, arrow keys move the marker, Space confirms
Click or press a number key to choose a form
Step 3: type or record (recordings play back inside the page only)
ui.childVariant: The scene becomes two adjoining rooms with animal characters, and the arrow is a sliding gift or ball. Use only one pair of forms (来/去, あげる/くれる, come/go). Do the action first, then say one sentence.
ui.adultVariant: Scenes come from work or daily life (a colleague handling something for you, moving house, borrowing things). Add the honorific layer (くださる, いただく) and the viewpoint of the passive-causative. Step 3 asks for a three- or four-sentence account with a consistent viewpoint throughout.
ui.accessibility: Characters and places in the scene all have text labels, and a screen reader reads "I am inside the room; the arrow points from outside the door into the room". The arrow direction is shown both by arrow shape and by text. Every drag has a keyboard alternative.

kcSignals: notions include space-motion or possession, or the label includes giving/receiving, coming/going, direction, passive or causative (kt:ja-ageru, kt:ja-kureru, kt:ja-morau, kt:ja-tekureru, kt:ja-teiku-tekuru, kt:ja-causative-passive-perspective, kt:zh-directional-simple, kt:zh-directional-compound, kt:zh-bei-passive)
commonErrors include "reversed direction relative to the speaker's position", "wrong reference point" or mixing the speaker's side and the other side
Switching subject and viewpoint back and forth within one narration is listed as an error
learnerSignals: Knows only one way to say "give" and "borrow"
When telling an experience, stands now on their own side and now on the other person's side
"Why use くれる here and not あげる?"
contraindications: The learner cannot yet inflect the form itself (e.g. forming the causative-passive); use prim:paradigm-apply first
The KC's viewpoint does not affect form choice (e.g. English give has no direction of its own); do not force a scene onto it
The learner does not yet know the words for the characters and places in the scene

rules: The Step 3 sentences must agree with the "I" position and arrows the learner set on the scene picture (form matches direction; blocks an answer that is too weak)

Step 3 needs at least one sentence toward "I" and one away from "I". Avoiding viewpoint by using a neutral form throughout (もらう all the way, "给" everywhere, give everywhere) does not pass (blocks gaming)
If the learner chooses "no change" on three Step 2 items in a row and some of those items should change, show the prompt "You may not be looking at where 'I' am"
check.independence: The first choice in Step 1 is recorded separately. A change of choice after seeing the connecting-line highlight or "the listener will think ..." is recorded as completed after a hint. Step 3 shows no model; only the scene the learner set up remains.

evidence.retained: For each item: where the learner placed "I", the arrow direction, the first form chosen and any revision, plus the Step 3 scene and the learner's own sentences, all kept on the same scene card

licensed.claim: Can choose the right form by viewpoint in a given scene
Can keep a consistent viewpoint in their own narration

prohibited: Judging viewpoint as mastered from correct Step 1 choices alone
Carrying correct scene-item choices over to continuous narration without a picture
Counting a correction made after seeing the "I" shadow position as independent
Carrying performance on giving/receiving over to coming/going or the passive (the three are recorded separately)

hints: Only ask "Where are you standing? Is the thing coming toward you or going away from you?"
Highlight "I" and the arrow's end point in the scene
Show two contrasting sentences for the same scene under the two viewpoints
scaffold.fade: After 4 items in a row on the same set of forms are first-attempt correct, the scene picture shrinks to a one-line text description and the draggable "I" marker is no longer offered

primitives.reverseHalf: Viewpoint is not always fixed by the speaker's physical position. English come can be anchored at the listener's location (I'll come to your party). In Japanese, the "our side" of くれる includes family and in-group members (妹にくれた), and between third parties あげる is the default. In Chinese, when the speaker is not present, "来/去" is anchored at the place under discussion. "被" is not the equivalent of the English passive; it is not used without an affected or disposed-of sense (*汉语被很多人说).

failureModes.failure: The learner memorizes "toward me = くれる / 来" and applies it mechanically, ignoring the extension to "our side" and the listener's viewpoint
failureModes.mitigation: Put into every set items where "our side" is family, and items where the viewpoint is at the listener
failureModes.test: In the adversarial set, one third of the items have "I" at neither end of the arrow

failureModes.failure: The scene picture gives the answer away, so the learner reads the picture and not the sentence
failureModes.mitigation: From Step 2 on, the learner places "I" from the text; the system does not pre-set it
failureModes.test: Compare accuracy with the picture removed (text only) against accuracy with the picture

failureModes.failure: Treating the passive or causative as a pure form conversion and ignoring the viewpoint of adversity or compulsion
failureModes.mitigation: Add items that pair a neutral passive and an adversity passive for the same event, and require the learner to say who is affected
failureModes.test: Check whether items like 雨に降られた / 被雨淋湿了 are treated as ordinary passives

stacksWith.how: On the same scene picture, first connect agent, recipient and source, then add the viewpoint arrow; the particles に/から and the giving/receiving verb are checked together
The arrow stays the same, and a politeness level is layered on the same sentence (くれる→くださる, もらう→いただく)
When retelling a story, the "I" marker follows the narrator, and every sentence must agree with the marker

languages.en: Contrast sets: come/go, bring/take, lend/borrow, choosing the viewpoint of active/passive. Traps: translating Chinese "来/去" literally and ignoring come anchored at the listener; subject reversal of lend/borrow (*Can you borrow me a pen?)
languages.ja: Contrast sets: あげる/くれる/もらう, てあげる/てくれる/てもらう, ていく/てくる, viewpoint of the passive (event, person, adversity) and the causative-passive. Traps: *友達が私にあげました, using くれる between third parties, writing 私に for *私の荷物, using させられた when meaning "got permission"
languages.zh: Contrast sets: 来/去, compound directional complements (上来/上去, 进来/进去, 回来/回去), the 被 sentence and notional passive. Traps: *他进来教室了 (position of the place object), saying 进去 while the speaker is inside, English speakers overusing 被, Japanese speakers transferring the adversity passive (*我被雨下了)

primitives.name: Clause-constraint check
primitives.oneLine: After choosing a connecting form for the first clause, judge what the main clause can be (request, volition, negation, past) and, when it is violated, point out which constraint it breaks
primitives.difficulty: Learners treat a connecting form as one translation ("if", "because", "as soon as"). They choose the right connector but do not know it constrains the main clause: *駅に着くと、電話してください, *家に帰ったとたん、シャワーを浴びるつもりです, *I'll call you when I will arrive, *In case it rains, we'll stay home (meaning "if"), *一他到家，就睡觉了, and 只有……才 swapped for 就. The error is not in the first clause. It is that the main clause was given a type it does not allow.
primitives.object: A two-slot sentence frame: the first clause is already written and carries the connecting form; the main clause is an empty slot. Beside it is a column of main-clause cards, each labeled with a type (request, volition, negation, past fact, general fact, evaluation).
primitives.requires: The learner can already attach the connecting form (attachment problems such as *安いだったら are solved first) and knows what the sentence patterns on the main-clause cards mean. If attachment is not yet known, fall back to prim:form-for-meaning.
learnerAction: Step 1 Try each card: the first clause and connecting form are fixed. Put the main-clause cards into the slot one by one and judge whether each can follow

Step 2 Swap the connector: the main clause is fixed. Replace the connecting form with another and judge whether the sentence still works; where it does not, name the constraint (locked options: the main-clause type is restricted (request, volition) / tense or time relation is restricted / the subjects of the two clauses are restricted / both work, only the meaning differs. The last option is the reverse half)
Step 3 Connect it yourself: given an everyday situation that must end with a request or volition, write the whole sentence yourself and choose the connecting form yourself
systemResponse: When a disallowed card is put in, the card bounces back to its place and the violated constraint appears above the frame ("と cannot be followed by a request"). It does not show "wrong".
After each judgment, one cell lights up in the sidebar table "what this connector allows". When a set is finished, the learner has a constraint table they filled in cell by cell.
When the connector is swapped in Step 2, the old and new sentences are kept side by side, and the two connectors' columns in the constraint table are compared side by side

ui.screen: At the top is the two-slot sentence frame, with the main-clause slot accepting cards. On the left is the column of main-clause cards (each card's type is shown by an icon and text). On the right is the constraint table: rows are main-clause types, columns are the connecting forms in this set, and the cells light up as "allowed / not allowed / undecided" as the learner works.
interactions: Drag a card into the slot, or select a card and press Enter to place it
Step 2: click a connecting-form button or press a number key to switch
Step 3: type; the main-clause type is detected by the system from the sentence ending and shown, and the learner can correct it
ui.childVariant: No constraint names. Use "story relay": the first half is paired with a picture and the second half has only two cards (one is "Please ...", one is "... happened"). Practice only one connecting form (一……就, when, たら).
ui.adultVariant: Situations come from work email and travel plans. The constraint table shows terms (volition, request, established fact). Step 3 asks for two sentences in the same situation, using two different connecting forms, both of which work.
ui.accessibility: Main-clause types are shown by icon and text together. The constraint table can be read row by row by a screen reader. Every drag has a keyboard alternative. On phones the constraint table folds into a button.

kcSignals: notions include condition, sequence, cause-reason or purpose (kt:ja-conditional-to, kt:ja-conditional-tara, kt:ja-conditional-ba, kt:ja-conditional-nara, kt:ja-conditional-family, kt:ja-totan, kt:ja-karaniwa, kt:ja-kara-node, kt:zh-zhiyao-jiu, kt:zh-yi-jiu, kt:zh-jishi-ye, kt:en-time-clauses, kt:en-conditional-alternatives)
commonErrors include main-clause restrictions such as "request or volition after the main clause", "will inside a subordinate clause", or "只有……才 replaced by 就"
itemTypes include recognize-choice and transform, and the KC is a connecting form
learnerSignals: Always translates "if" as たら or if
The first clause is right but the main clause keeps being corrected
"Why can't I use と here?"
contraindications: The attachment of the connecting form is not yet mastered (*学生たら); practice attachment first
The difference between two connecting forms is mainly about intent, not constraints (the sequence relation of たら vs. なら); use prim:choose-by-intent first
The problem is only a missing word in a fixed pattern (leaving out "就"); prim:form-for-meaning or prim:slot-order is more direct

rules: The Step 3 main clause must be of the type the situation requires (detected from the sentence ending: てください / つもり / ましょう, please / let's, 吧 / 请), and the connecting form must be in that type's allowed set (blocks an answer that is too weak)

If in Step 3 the learner always uses an all-purpose form (たら, if, 如果) to avoid constraints, the second half of the task gives a situation where the all-purpose form is unnatural (preparation before departure takes なら). Not switching forms does not pass (blocks gaming).
If in Step 1 the learner judges the same card "allowed" under two connectors, they must give the reason on the Step 2 constraint table, otherwise it is not recorded as passed
check.independence: The first judgment in Step 1 is recorded separately. Placing a card correctly after seeing the constraint name is recorded as completed after a hint. The constraint table is folded in Step 3, and opening it is recorded as asking for help.

evidence.retained: For each main-clause card under each connector: the first judgment and any revised judgment, the constraint table the learner filled in, and the Step 3 whole sentence with its detected main-clause type, all kept on the same sentence-frame set

licensed.claim: Can judge whether a sentence type is allowed after a given connecting form
Can actively avoid a restricted connecting form when a request or volition must close the sentence

prohibited: Judging that the learner can use a form because the constraint table was filled in correctly
Carrying performance on one connecting form over to the other forms in the set
Counting a correct placement after seeing the constraint name as independent
Treating a grammatically correct main clause as proof that the connecting form was chosen correctly

hints: Only ask "Is the second half asking the other person to do something, saying what you plan to do, or saying something that already happened?"
Light up the type icon on the main-clause card
Show a minimal contrast pair for that connecting form, one allowed and one not allowed
scaffold.fade: After 4 cards in a row on the same connecting form are first-attempt correct, the type icons on the main-clause cards are hidden and the learner must judge the type themselves

primitives.reverseHalf: The constraints are not absolute. At least one item per set breaks the surface rule. と can be followed by a past fact when narrating the past (ドアを開けると、猫がいた). When the first clause of ば is a stative predicate, the main clause can take volition (安ければ買います). ので is more appropriate than から in a polite request. English when can take will when it introduces a noun clause or a question (I don't know when he will arrive). In Chinese, 只要……就 and 只有……才 cannot be swapped, but where both work, the meanings are opposite.

failureModes.failure: The learner looks only at whether the main-clause ending has "ください / please" and ignores the connecting form
failureModes.mitigation: Add cards whose ending is a request but quoted, so it is actually reported speech, and cards with an unmarked volition sentence
failureModes.test: In the adversarial set, one quarter of the main-clause types cannot be judged from the final word of the sentence

failureModes.failure: Over-generalizing to "nothing can follow と"
failureModes.mitigation: Reverse-half items take at least two items in every set
failureModes.test: Check the learner's false-rejection rate on allowed cards

failureModes.failure: The type label on the main-clause card gives the answer away directly
failureModes.mitigation: Hide the labels from Step 2 and withdraw them gradually under the fade condition
failureModes.test: Compare first-attempt accuracy with and without labels

stacksWith.how: For the conditional family, first choose the form by intent in the same sentence frame, then check the main-clause constraint on that same frame
When two short sentences are joined into one, the main clause being attached is checked against the constraint table at the same time
For items like たとたん / 一……就 / as soon as, a timeline is layered under the sentence frame, and the gap between the two events is shown in sync

languages.en: Connecting forms: time clauses introduced by when / as soon as / until (present tense for the future in the clause), if / unless / provided / as long as / in case. Traps: *when I will arrive, in case used as if, adding another negative after unless, understanding not … until, writing *As long as…, so… by copying Chinese "只要……就"
languages.ja: Connecting forms: と / たら / ば / なら, たとたん, からには, べく, たりとも, ので / から. Traps: request or volition after と and ば, volition after たとたん (*帰ったとたん…つもりです), using なら for time sequence, using から when making a request of a superior sounds like an excuse; べく and たりとも are advanced written forms whose main clause is mostly volition or negation
languages.zh: Connecting forms: 只要……就 / 只有……才, 一……就, 即使……也, 既然……就, 如果……就. Traps: mixing 只有……就, leaving out "就" or "也", putting "一" before the subject, the main clause after 既然 carries an inference or suggestion and cannot carry a plain fact

primitives.name: Oral-to-print linking
primitives.oneLine: Start from words the learner can already say, link the sound and meaning directly to the written form, then recognize it in new combinations
primitives.difficulty: Learners can say far more words than they can recognize in print. A Chinese heritage child abroad says "冰箱" and "下雨了" without hesitation but cannot recognize those characters. The textbook starts over from "你好" and pinyin, which is boring and wastes the spoken Chinese they already have. A young English learner can say apple and banana but does not know which string of letters on the page is the word. What is missing is not sound or meaning. It is the step of attaching the existing sound-and-meaning directly to the written shape. Learning pinyin first and characters afterward adds an extra detour.
primitives.object: A sentence or set of words the learner said themselves, recorded as an "my words" card (with a picture the learner chose). Written text appears on the card step by step and builds up into a personal word-recognition wall.
primitives.requires: Can say and understand the target word aloud. If the word is not yet in the learner's speech, fall back to prim:scene-walkthrough to build the spoken word first. Pinyin or phonetic symbols are not required.
learnerAction: Step 1 Say it: look at a picture of daily life or talk about something that happened today, and say one sentence. The system (or a parent or teacher) writes it as text under the picture. The learner listens to the playback while following the characters with a finger.

Step 2 Recognize it: the same character or word appears in a new combination (冰箱→冰淇淋, 下雨→下午; apple→an apple pie). From three word cards the learner taps the one they have said, and judges whether it means the same in the new combination (locked options: same character, same meaning / same character, meaning changed / looks similar but is not the same character. The last option is the reverse half, e.g. 大/太, was/saw).

Step 3 Read it to someone: take a new sentence card with no picture and no phonetic aid and read it to a parent, partner or teacher. The learner may also record it first and check it by playing it back.
systemResponse: What was said in Step 1 appears as text on the learner's own picture. Each character can be tapped, and tapping plays the learner's own recording of that part (not a standard pronunciation).

Each time a character is recognized in Step 2, the "times met" count at the bottom right of its card goes up by one, and on the recognition wall the character is linked to every word it has appeared in
A wrong choice is not marked wrong. Two cards (the chosen character and the one being looked for) are shown side by side, each with its own picture, and the learner chooses again

ui.screen: On the left are the learner's picture and the "my words" card. On the right is the recognition wall (organized by the learner's own words, not by textbook order). In Step 2 three word cards appear below. No pinyin or phonetic symbols are shown.
interactions: Tap a character to play a recording; hold the record key to speak (recordings stay inside the page and are not scored automatically)
Tap or drag a word card; by keyboard, arrow keys select a card and Enter confirms
Step 3 has a "ask a partner to listen" confirmation button, and the listener taps "understood / did not understand"
ui.childVariant: For ages 5–8: pictures come from the child's home, pets and toys, with at most three new characters at a time. The recognition wall is a tree, and each recognition grows a leaf. Reading to a parent is the main activity, and there is no writing requirement.
ui.adultVariant: For adult heritage speakers who have spoken language, or teenagers raised abroad: topics come from family, work, menus and text messages. Step 2 adds homophones written differently (在/再, 的/得) and written words replacing spoken words (啥→什么).
ui.accessibility: Font size is adjustable and large by default. Tap-to-read highlights the current character. The record button has a text label. On phones the recognition wall scrolls sideways.

kcSignals: The learning track assumes spoken language but not literacy (e.g. zh-heritage-kids, en young-early)
itemTypes include script-reading or read-aloud, and the KC is a basic character or sight word (kt:zh-hanzi-l1, kt:zh-hanzi-l2, kt:en-orth-sight-words)
commonErrors include "long reliance on pinyin, unable to read characters without pinyin" or reversal of similar-looking sight words
learnerSignals: Can say it but cannot recognize it
A parent says "He understands everything, he just doesn't recognize characters"
Reads when pinyin is there and cannot once it is covered
contraindications: The learner does not have these words in speech (adult beginners); enter from prim:sound-spelling-blend or prim:character-anatomy
When the goal is writing rather than recognition, use prim:character-anatomy
When home speech is a dialect and the words correspond poorly to written Mandarin characters, they cannot be used directly as cards

rules: Step 2 must be recognized correctly at least once with no picture, no pinyin and the card positions shuffled (blocks gaming: guessing from the picture, remembering position)
A learner who can recognize only the whole word and fails in another combination is not recorded as recognizing this character (blocks an answer that is too weak)
Step 3 needs a real listener's confirmation or the learner's self-judgment on playback. The system does not score pronunciation and records only "who understood".
check.independence: Pointing along with the playback in Step 1 does not count as recognition. The first tap in Step 2 is recorded separately, and tapping after playing the recording is recorded as after a hint. In Step 3 the listener marks whether any prompting happened midway.

evidence.retained: For each character: the first recognition (with or without picture, with or without hint), times met and the combinations it has appeared in, all kept on the learner's recognition wall. The Step 3 recording and the listener's marks are kept on the sentence card.

licensed.claim: Can recognize this character or word, already in their speech, with no picture and no phonetic aid
Can recognize this character in a combination not seen before
Can read words from their own speech aloud as a sentence

prohibited: Inferring that the learner can write the character from recognition
Inferring that the learner can read written texts from recognizing spoken words
Recording a reading made after a parent's prompt as independent
Automatically scoring pronunciation or tone

hints: Only ask "In which sentence did you say this character?"
Play the learner's own recording of that character
Show beside it again the picture where this character appeared
scaffold.fade: After the same character is recognized on first attempt in three different combinations, remove its picture from the recognition wall and leave only the character

primitives.reverseHalf: Speech and writing do not correspond one to one. Homophones need no distinction in speech but must be distinguished in writing (在/再, 他/她/它). The written form of a spoken word may differ (啥, 咋, gonna, wanna). Dialect words spoken at home (Cantonese "冇", "佢") are not Mandarin written characters. Many familiar spoken English words have irregular spelling (said, one, come), so the sound cannot be guessed from the letters.

failureModes.failure: The learner guesses from the picture or card position instead of recognizing the character
failureModes.mitigation: In Step 2, remove the picture, shuffle positions, and add similar-looking distractor characters from the same set
failureModes.test: Compare first-attempt accuracy without pictures to accuracy with pictures; if the gap is large, do not record the character as recognized

failureModes.failure: Recognizes only the shape of the whole word and fails once it is taken apart
failureModes.mitigation: The same character must be recognized in at least two different combinations
failureModes.test: In the adversarial set, the target character appears in new words the learner has never said

failureModes.failure: A parent reads for the child or prompts too much
failureModes.mitigation: The listener's marking screen in Step 3 requires ticking "did you help midway?"
failureModes.test: Spot-check whether the recordings and the marks agree

stacksWith.how: Break the same word card into components, and use characters the learner already recognizes to introduce new characters with the same component
English direction: on the same "my words" card, match the first sound to the first letter, so spoken words become the starting point for blending
For learners who need phonetic aid, the aid appears on the same card only as the last level of hint and is removed character by character as they master it

languages.en: Target: picture words and classroom language that young learners can already say (apple, dog, look, come). Traps: sounding out sight words by force (said read as /seɪd/), reversal of similar-looking words (was/saw, on/no), confusing the/they
languages.ja: Target: words already spoken by heritage children who speak Japanese or by anime fans (ありがとう, かわいい, たべる). Attach hiragana first, then attach kanji to the kun-reading words already spoken (たべる→食べる). Trap: spoken contractions (ちゃう, じゃん) differ from the written form
languages.zh: Target: high-frequency words in a heritage child's home speech (冰箱, 下雨, 吃饭, 妈妈). Pinyin is not required first. Traps: homophone substitution (*我明天在来), similar-looking characters (人/入, 大/太), dialect spoken words with no standard character, and overseas families may use traditional characters, so the target form must be fixed first

primitives.name: Phonological awareness play
primitives.oneLine: Without looking at text, rhyme, clap syllables, and split and swap phonemes using sound alone
primitives.difficulty: Without text, learners cannot tell how many syllables, beats or phonemes a word has. Chinese-speaking children split by initial plus final, so cat is cut only as c-at, and a vowel is automatically added after a consonant (/b/ read as bu). Chinese speakers learning Japanese count とうきょう as two beats by Chinese syllables, and the geminate, long vowel and ん are swallowed. Heritage children abroad can say "妈" but do not know it differs from "马" only in tone, and they lack this awareness later when they turn to pinyin and dictionary look-up.
primitives.object: A set of picture words (only sound and picture, no text). Under each word is a row of lightable sound blocks. The same set of words is used repeatedly across the three steps.
primitives.requires: Knows the spoken word the picture stands for and can listen to the audio on the page. Literacy is not required.
learnerAction: Step 1 Tap it out: listen to a word and, for each syllable heard (a beat in Japanese, a phoneme at the advanced English level), clap once or light one box. The number of boxes is the answer.

Step 2 Swap it: replace or remove the first sound, the last sound or a certain beat of the word, and judge which picture it becomes (or that it is not a word). Then sort pairs of words (locked options: rhyme / same first sound / same number of beats / none of these. The reverse half is pairs that "look alike but do not rhyme by sound" and pairs that "differ only in tone").
Step 3 Find your own: say a word that rhymes with the target word, starts the same, or has the same number of beats. A partner listens, or the learner records it and checks by playing it back.
systemResponse: When the learner taps boxes, the boxes light up in sync with the audio. When the beat count is wrong, the playback slows down so that each beat falls on one box, and the learner sees where they clapped too many or too few.
After a sound swap, the picture changes to the picture of the new word. When the swap does not make a word, an empty frame is shown with "this swap does not make a word".
After sorting, a line is drawn between the two pictures, linking the part of the sound blocks they share (the final boxes, the first box, or the whole row count)

ui.screen: A large picture is in the middle with a row of empty sound-block boxes (up to 6) below it. Play and slow-play buttons are at the bottom. In Step 2 two pictures appear side by side. No letters, kana, pinyin or characters appear at any point.
interactions: Tap a box or press the space bar to clap once; on a touch screen the learner can tap the screen directly
Drag a small sound block onto a box to mean replacement
Play and slow-play are unlimited; recordings play back only inside the page and are not scored automatically
ui.childVariant: For ages 5–7: use clapping and hopscotch animations, with words from animals and food. Do one operation per set (only rhyme, or only clapping syllables). A teacher or parent is the listener in Step 3.
ui.adultVariant: For adults learning Japanese: dedicated beat-sense practice, with words from place names and loanwords (とうきょう, コーヒー, きって). For English, phoneme segmentation for adults who need to correct "adding vowels". The names for beat, syllable and phoneme may be shown.
ui.accessibility: Sound-block boxes change in both brightness and border. Every action has sound feedback. A screen reader reads "box 2 tapped". Playback speed is adjustable.

kcSignals: The KC label includes phonemic awareness, rhyme, mora, geminate, long vowel or contracted sound (kt:en-phon-awareness, kt:ja-sound-mora, kt:ja-sound-sokuon, kt:ja-sound-long, kt:ja-sound-yoon)
commonErrors include adding a vowel after a consonant, splitting by initial and final, swallowing long vowels and geminates, and splitting contracted sounds into two beats
The learning track is for young children who cannot read yet (en young-early) or heritage children who can speak but not read (zh-heritage-kids)
learnerSignals: A vowel is attached after every consonant when blending
Dictation drops っ and long vowels
Cannot answer "How many sounds does this word have?"
contraindications: The learner can already blend reliably and the problem is hearing one particular pair of sounds; use prim:sound-contrast
When it must be judged whether pronunciation is standard, this primitive does not score; use prim:record-self-transcribe or a real listener
Learners with hearing impairment need a visual or tactile beat instead and cannot use this directly

rules: No text appears at any point, so that answers cannot be based on the number of characters or letters (blocks gaming)

In each set, at least half of the words have a sound-block count that differs from the likely character count (きょう is two beats and three kana, cake is three phonemes and four letters, とうきょう is four beats and two kanji). Learners who count only characters or letters fail on these items (blocks gaming).
The word said in Step 3 must be confirmed by a partner or self-judged by the learner on playback, and must not be a word that already appeared in the task (blocks an answer that is too weak)
check.independence: The first beat count in Step 1 is recorded separately. Tapping again after hearing slow play is recorded as completed after a hint. In Step 3, record who the listener was (partner, parent, self on playback).

evidence.retained: For each word: the first beat count and the count after slow play, the result of each swap operation, the sorting lines, and the Step 3 recording and listener's mark, all kept on the same set of picture words

licensed.claim: Can count the syllables or beats of a word without looking at text
Can rhyme, change first sounds or swap phonemes in spoken words
Can produce a rhyming or same-beat word that meets the requirement on their own

prohibited: Inferring that the duration of the learner's pronunciation is accurate because they can count beats
Automatically scoring the learner's pronunciation or judging accent
Inferring that the learner can blend from success at phoneme operations
Recording a correct tap after seeing slow play as independent

hints: Only say "Listen again and clap along"
Play the slow version, with a pause between beats
Demonstrate the clapping with a word of the same structure that the learner already knows
scaffold.fade: After 5 words in a row of the same kind of operation are first-attempt correct, remove the slow-play button and keep only normal-speed playback

primitives.reverseHalf: Rhyme depends on sound, not spelling. though and through do not rhyme, blue and two do. In Japanese a beat is not a syllable: ん, っ and a long vowel each take one beat but cannot form a syllable alone (とうきょう is four beats and two syllables). Chinese rhyme looks only at the final, not the tone (妈/马 rhyme), but a different tone means a different meaning. Rhyme and homophony are two different things.

failureModes.failure: The learner claps by how long the meaning is or how big the picture is
failureModes.mitigation: Include words with a short meaning and long sound (elephant) and a long meaning and short sound (car)
failureModes.test: In the adversarial set, the size of the meaning is unrelated to the beat count

failureModes.failure: Folds Japanese long vowels and geminates into the previous beat by Chinese rhythm
failureModes.mitigation: Every set has minimal pairs that differ by only one special beat (きて/きって, おばさん/おばあさん)
failureModes.test: Count first-attempt accuracy on special-beat items

failureModes.failure: Children imitate only the teacher's clapping rhythm instead of listening to the word
failureModes.mitigation: No demonstration animation is shown while audio plays; the demonstration appears only at hint level 3
failureModes.test: Compare accuracy with and without the demonstration

stacksWith.how: The minimal pairs produced by the swaps in Step 2 serve directly as discrimination material, with the differing box marked on the same row of sound blocks
Japanese direction: put the words whose boxes are tapped back into a sentence to shadow, and the same row of boxes extends into the beat of the whole sentence
After literacy, attach letters or kana one by one to the boxes on the same row of sound blocks

languages.en: Operations: rhyme, clapping syllables, onset-rime (c-at), phoneme segmentation and substitution (cat→hat→hot). Traps: adding a vowel after a consonant (/b/→bu), cutting into only two parts by initial and final, dropping a final consonant or adding a vowel (bed→bede)
languages.ja: Operations: counting beats, especially geminates, long vowels, the moraic nasal and contracted sounds (きって, とうきょう, ほん, きょう). Traps: counting とうきょう as two beats by Chinese syllables, splitting contracted sounds into two beats, swallowing long vowels (おばあさん→おばさん)
languages.zh: Operations: counting syllables, finding rhymes (same final), hearing the same syllable in different tones. For heritage children, do not teach pinyin symbols first; do only sound operations. Traps: treating rhyme as homophony, letting sentence intonation override word tone under the influence of English

primitives.name: Reading selection
primitives.oneLine: For a character or word in the current context, choose its reading (on/kun reading, polyphonic character, heteronym) and state the basis
primitives.difficulty: One written form has several readings, and the learner remembers only one and applies it everywhere. In Japanese, "生" is read only せい, 土産 is read *どさん, 大人 is read *だいじん, 一人 is read *いちにん, and rendaku is missed where it belongs (*てかみ) or applied everywhere (*あいがぎ). In Chinese, "还书" is read hái shū, "长大" is read cháng dà, and "得" is always read de. In English, the present and past of read, verb and noun lead, and REcord vs. reCORD are not distinguished. What is missing is the step "look at word formation and context first, then decide the reading".
primitives.object: A short passage in which 3–6 same-form characters or words are marked, each with a reading slot above it. The passage stays the same across the three steps, and the reading slots fill in gradually.
primitives.requires: Already recognizes at least one reading and the meaning of the character or word. If the whole passage needs phonetic aid to be read, fall back to prim:reading-aid-fade first.
learnerAction: Step 1 Read first, then decide: choose a reading for each marked spot and choose one basis (locked bases: part of speech or tense / a fixed phrase or compound it sits in / the number or counter before it / the sounds around it (rendaku) / no rule, must be remembered separately. The last option is the reverse half).
Step 2 Change the sentence: put the same written form into another sentence and judge whether the reading changes and which basis applies.
Step 3 Make your own: write a sentence in which the same written form appears twice with different readings (我还要还书, 今日は今日（こんにち）の…, I read it last week and I'll read it again), and mark both readings.
systemResponse: After a reading is chosen, the audio for that spot plays. The first choice is kept in a small label above the reading slot, and a later change does not overwrite it.
