The types of trouble moment are written in advance and known, so even an open conversation can be checked. What is checked is not the content of what the learner says but which kind of repair move was made at this moment and whether the wording was appropriate. The page does not generate the other person's lines and does not automatically score the learner's speech.
primitives.requires: Can already carry through the main line of the exchange script (see prim:exchange-script) and can already call up a few repair phrases (see prim:recall-before-reveal). If not a single repair phrase can be said, go back first.
learnerAction: Step 1 Repair on the spot: when a trouble moment arrives while the script plays, the learner makes one repair move within the time window (beginners choose from options; intermediate and above say it or type it and label the type themselves): ask for repetition / ask the other person to slow down / ask about a word / restate to confirm / back-channel and take up the talk / buy time to think / interrupt politely / pull the topic back. Doing nothing, or saying only "是的", is also recorded as a choice.

Step 2 Review: replay each trouble moment one by one and judge your own move by locked categories: matched the trouble type / right type but abrupt wording / pretended to understand (only back-channeled, did not repair) / no interruption was actually needed here. The last is the reverse half: a word the other person is about to explain, or a detail unrelated to the task, can be let go, and over-repair also interrupts the exchange.

Step 3 Do it independently in a different conversation: in a new script or a conversation with a live partner, turn off the options and say the repair sentences yourself. The live partner's role card notes at the marked spots "speak very fast here / use this new word / stay silent for five seconds", and a checklist records which kind of repair the learner used and whether it was appropriate.
systemResponse: After a repair move, the other person gives a pre-written response by move type: asked to slow down, they repeat slowly; asked about a word, they explain that word; when the learner restates to confirm and the number in the restatement is wrong, the other person corrects it, so the learner sees what restating to confirm does

When the learner does nothing or only back-channels, the conversation goes on as usual, but at the end the task goes wrong (the wrong time was arranged, the wrong thing was bought), and the ending card traces back and marks the trouble moment where it was planted
In the review, each trouble moment is shown as a marker on the conversation timeline, with the learner's first move and several appropriate wordings of that type listed beside it

ui.screen: At the top are the conversation bubble stream and the other person's recording. When a trouble moment arrives, a row of repair-move buttons lights up at the bottom (in a fixed order) with a countdown bar without numbers. On the right is the conversation timeline, where trouble moments are replayable markers.
interactions: Number keys choose the repair move, and Space pauses (the number of pauses is recorded)
R records, or type directly, then click a type label to self-label
In review, use the left/right arrow keys to jump between trouble moments
ui.childVariant: Only two or three kinds of trouble (said too fast, an unknown word, did not hear clearly), and two or three fixed repair phrases, with gesture pictures (ear = say it again, snail = slower). No time window. In Step 3 the teacher plays the other person.
ui.adultVariant: Scenes such as phone calls, meetings and clinic visits, adding interrupting, pulling the topic back, buying time and summarizing others' views. The time window is close to a real pause length. Step 3 is done with a live partner and requires at least one restatement to confirm.
ui.accessibility: The text of each of the other person's lines can be shown, but completing with text on is recorded as assisted. The time window can be turned off (and is then recorded as an untimed condition). Nothing depends on color.

kcSignals: notions include interaction-management

The KC is conversation repair and back-channeling (kt:en-str-repair-basic, kt:en-str-ask-clarification, kt:en-fn-check-understanding, kt:en-fn-manage-turns, kt:en-str-gain-time, kt:en-informal-spoken-markers, kt:ja-str-repair-basic, kt:ja-str-aizuchi, kt:zh-str-repair-basic, kt:zh-fn-discussion)
commonErrors include "saying only Yes / はい to pretend to understand", "*What? sounds impolite" and "Chinese 'that' carried into the target language"
itemTypes include role-play
learnerSignals: Nods without understanding
Stays silent for a long time while the other person is speaking
"I don't know how to interrupt people"
The teacher says "As soon as they don't understand they freeze"
contraindications: The main-line script itself cannot yet be completed
The target is the argument content in a formal discussion and not interaction management (use prim:discourse-map)
It cannot be used to assess pronunciation or listening level itself

rules: The type of repair move must match the trouble type and the wording must be appropriate (*What?, a falling-tone え？ and *你是什么意思？ do not count). A restatement to confirm must include the key information (that number, that word) (blocks an answer that is too weak).
Handling every moment with the same Sorry?, or interrupting at moments where no interruption is needed, is judged as not distinguishing trouble types (blocks gaming)

For repairs said in open speech, three parties judge: the learner's self-labelled type, comparison with the list of appropriate wordings for that type, and the live partner's tick. The system does not score automatically.
check.independence: The first move at each trouble moment, including "no action", is recorded separately. A move made after pausing, turning on the text, or viewing the review checklist is recorded as assisted. Step 3 counts only new conversations without options. Anything the partner prompted is marked as assisted on the checklist.

evidence.retained: For each trouble moment: its type, the learner's first move (including no move), whether the reaction fell within the time window, the self-judged category in review, the recording or text and the partner's checklist in Step 3, and the trace-back on the ending card

licensed.claim: Can recognize a moment that needs repair in a controlled conversation and make the right kind of repair move
Can complete a repair independently with an appropriate wording in a new conversation

prohibited: Inferring that the learner will repair in real conversation from repair performance in a script
Inferring that the learner understood from a lot of back-channeling (はい and 嗯 do not equal understanding or agreement)
Inferring a high listening level from fluent repair phrases
Automatically scoring speech in repair recordings

hints: Pause and only ask "Where did you lose track just now?"
Show the name of the trouble type (too fast / new word / number / waiting for you to take over)
Show two or three appropriate wordings for this type
scaffold.fade: After 3 times in a row on the same kind of trouble with the first move being the right type and appropriate, that kind no longer shows its type name. The time window is changed from loose to close to real after two conversations.

primitives.reverseHalf: Not every failure to understand needs an interruption: a word the other person will explain in the next sentence and a detail unrelated to the task can be let go. Every conversation has at least one moment where "no interruption is needed". The other half is listening in reverse: the other person's はい, ええ and 嗯 are often only "I'm listening" and cannot be taken as acceptance or agreement.

failureModes.failure: The learner copes with all trouble using one all-purpose Sorry?
failureModes.mitigation: Design moments that only a specific repair can advance (when asking about a word's meaning, repeating it does not help and the learner must ask about that word)
failureModes.test: Adversarial sample: a path using the same repair every time cannot complete the task

failureModes.failure: The buttons light up as soon as a trouble moment appears, so the learner knows "now is the time to repair" without listening
failureModes.mitigation: The button row is available throughout the conversation, and some "false trouble" moments need no repair
failureModes.test: Compare the trigger rate at real trouble moments and at false ones

failureModes.failure: A live partner does not create trouble as the role card says, or says it for the learner
failureModes.mitigation: The role card spells out how to do each trouble moment, and the checklist records "the partner gave a prompt" separately
failureModes.test: Spot-check whether the partner checklist agrees with the recording

stacksWith.how: Trouble moments are inserted straight into the same turn tree, and the branch without repair leads to an ending where the task goes wrong
A trouble moment where numbers are given requires restating to confirm, and the restated numbers are entered in the same information grid and checked
In review, write down the sentence that was not heard clearly and align it word by word with the original to see where the sound changed

languages.en: Repair phrases: Sorry? / Pardon? / Could you say that again, please? / Could you speak a bit more slowly? / What does X mean? / So you mean…? / Sorry to interrupt, but… / Anyway, as I was saying… / Well, let me think… Traps: *What?, *Please repeat, *Again, *What is mean…?, *I no understand, saying Chinese "那个" as *that…, saying only Yes to pretend to understand, *Do you understand me? sounding condescending
languages.ja: Repair phrases: すみません、もう一度お願いします / もう少しゆっくりお願いします / ～って何ですか / ～ということですか. Back-channels: はい・ええ・そうですか・なるほど (use with care toward superiors)・うん (close relationships). Fillers: えーと・あのう. Traps: a falling-tone え？なに？, silence or only はい taken as understood, saying うん to a teacher, filling gaps with Chinese "那个", taking the other person's はい as agreement
languages.zh: Repair phrases: 请再说一遍 / 请说慢一点儿 / “X”是什么意思？ / 你的意思是……吗？. Back-channels: 嗯、对、是吗、然后呢. Interrupting: 不好意思，我插一句. Pulling back: 我们回到刚才的问题. English-speaker traps: *请说再一遍, *请一点儿慢说, *请又说一遍; a follow-up question said as *你是什么意思？; using "等等！" on formal occasions

primitives.name: Writing on a real template
primitives.oneLine: Fill in or write a short text on a real format (form, note, message, email template), where every field constrains what to write
primitives.difficulty: The real format is itself the rule, but the learner writes by mother-tongue habit. The family name goes into First name, and a date written year-month-day is ambiguous. Furigana is written in hiragana or pinyin, and names in simplified forms (刘, 张) do not match the identity document. A note leaves out the addressee or signature, or adds さん after the writer's own name. An email to a teacher gives no name, writes a long background first and says what is wanted only at the end, uses ～てください like an order, or doubles up honorifics (*山田先生様). A chat opens with "在吗？" (*Are you there?) and does not say the matter. A Chinese text message picks the wrong homophone through pinyin (*我明天在来), and the reply to a teacher is only "嗯" or "哦".
primitives.object: A blank template in a real format (sign-up form, registration form, note, message card, chat interface, email template), plus a situation card (who you are, who you are writing to, what you want the other person to do, the specific information). Every field or position of the template has its own constraint. The first draft, the field-by-field check and the rewrite for a different recipient all take place on this template. The situation card uses a fictional identity and does not collect the learner's real personal information.
primitives.requires: Can read the field names of this kind of format (see prim:real-document-scan) and can write the required text (for character or kana forms, see prim:character-anatomy). If the field names cannot be read, go back first.
learnerAction: Step 1 Write first: following the situation card, fill in the form or write the message directly, and save the first draft.

Step 2 Check field by field: for each field or position, expand its constraint (what the person reading this field does with it, what format it needs, what character form to use, where it goes), and judge your own entry field by field: acceptable / content right but format wrong / put in the wrong field / missing. The last category is the reverse half: this field may be left blank, or this sentence may be left out.

Step 3 Rewrite for a different recipient or a different format: write the same matter again for a different recipient (friend → teacher → unknown organization), or on a form with different fields, without expanding the constraints.
systemResponse: During the field-by-field check, the consequences are shown from the reader's point of view. When the date is written 05/06, "will be read as May 6" and "will be read as June 5" are shown side by side, and the name field shows "who the person processing the form will take to be your family name".

An email or message template simulates the recipient's preview: a phone notification shows only the first two lines, so a request written last cannot be seen in the preview. When a note has no signature, the recipient's view shows "who wrote this?".

Constraints a machine can check (date format, whether furigana is katakana, whether required fields are empty, whether both salutation and signature are present, whether the request sentence appears in the first two sentences) are marked on the spot. Whether the register is appropriate is not judged automatically and is left to the Step 3 comparison.

ui.screen: On the left is the template, keeping its original layout, and on the right is the situation card. In Step 2 an expandable constraint label and judgment buttons appear beside each field. At the top, the view switches between "what I wrote" and "what the recipient sees".
interactions: Tab moves between fields and the learner types directly
Number keys choose the judgment category, and Enter expands or collapses the constraint
On phones the template is a single column, and the recipient preview is shown as a phone notification
ui.childVariant: A library borrowing card, a birthday invitation, a note left for family. Only three or four fields, with an icon hinting what each field needs. Writing can use spelling cards. The judgment has only two options, "written right / still missing".
ui.adultVariant: A sign-up form, rental registration, a leave-of-absence email, a message to a teacher or client, a text to reschedule. Asks for the same matter to be written to two kinds of recipients, with an explanation of how the two versions differ.
ui.accessibility: Each field has a readable label and constraint note. The recipient view also has a text description. Problems are not marked by color alone.

kcSignals: The KC is filling in a form or writing a short message (kt:en-skill-write-forms, kt:en-skill-write-messages, kt:en-skill-digital-messaging, kt:ja-skill-write-forms-memo, kt:ja-skill-write-messages, kt:ja-skill-write-email-polite, kt:zh-skill-write-basic, kt:zh-skill-write-messages)
itemTypes include form-fill and situated-production-written
commonErrors include format problems with fields, dates, character forms, salutation and signature, or the order of the request
learnerSignals: The teacher does not know who wrote the email to them
Family and given names are filled in reversed on forms
Nothing follows after "在吗？"
contraindications: The field names still cannot be read
The target is extended argument or a report, where the format is only a shell (use prim:discourse-map or prim:grow-text)
Do not let learners write their real identity-document information into the page

rules: All required fields are filled in and meet the machine-checkable format constraints (date unambiguous, furigana in katakana, name fields not swapped relative to the situation card, a salutation and a signature present, the request in the first two sentences) (blocks an answer that is too weak)

The filled-in content must correspond to the specific information on the situation card. Copying the template's example or filling in an all-purpose sentence does not count. The message must contain the request or conclusion the situation requires, and writing only background does not count (blocks gaming).
Between the two versions in Step 3 there must be changes in salutation, register and the way the request is stated that fit the recipient. Two identical versions are judged not passed.
check.independence: The first draft is locked before any constraint is expanded. A revision made after expanding the constraint of a field or viewing a model of the same kind is recorded as completed after a hint. Step 3 does not expand constraints and does not show models.

evidence.retained: The first draft, the field-by-field judgments and which constraints were expanded, the revised draft, the Step 3 rewrite for a different recipient or format and the comparison of the two versions

licensed.claim: Can complete this kind of format according to its constraints
Can adjust the format and register of a short message to the recipient

prohibited: Inferring that the language is correct from an acceptable format
Inferring that the learner can fill in any form from being able to fill in one kind
Inferring that the learner can do it when dealing with a real organization from performance on a simulated template

hints: Only ask "What will the person reading this field do with it?"
Expand the constraint note for this field
Show a completed example of the same kind in a different situation
scaffold.fade: After two first drafts in a row of the same kind of format have every field acceptable, constraint expansion is no longer provided and models are no longer shown

primitives.reverseHalf: A more complete format is not always more formal or better: a message to a friend needs no 拝啓 or Dear Sir, and a note does not need all the parts of a letter. Some fields may be left blank or filled with "无/なし/N/A". A chat message that states the matter directly is more appropriate than one built up with greetings. In at least one item per set the correct action is to leave something out or leave it blank.

failureModes.failure: The learner copies the model or the example values in the template
failureModes.mitigation: The specific information on the situation card is different each time, and the values filled in are checked against the situation card
failureModes.test: Adversarial sample: a draft that copies the model must be judged not passed

failureModes.failure: The format is all correct but the register does not suit the recipient
failureModes.mitigation: Step 3 forces a change of recipient and compares the two versions

languages.en: Format: Surname / First name, writing the month as a word to avoid the DD/MM vs. MM/DD ambiguity, the Nationality field; notes and postcards Dear Sam, … Love, / Best,; a message states the matter directly, does not open with *Are you there?, and does not use u / thx to a superior; formal email Dear Mr Smith (*Dear Mr. John), I look forward to hearing from you
languages.ja: Format: フリガナ (katakana) vs. ふりがな (hiragana), name character forms matching the identity document (劉, 張), addresses written from large to small, 〒, the Japanese era calendar; a note names the recipient and does not add さん after the writer's own name; an email first gives the sender's name and states the matter first, uses ～ていただけないでしょうか rather than ～てください, does not double honorifics (*山田先生様), and replies with 承知しました / わかりました rather than 了解です
languages.zh: Format: name and date of birth in year-month-day order, standard simplified character forms (Japanese speakers' 対→对, 歩→步); a note needs a salutation, body, signature and date; in text messages watch for homophones (再/在); to a teacher, open with the salutation "老师您好" and give your name, and do not reply with only "嗯" or "哦"
